text:
离 0.4 不远了，#ENA。

现在上车，真到了 0.4，可能就是别人来给你抬轿子了。

为什么最近 ENA 这么猛？

别只看 K 线，去看看 Ethena 的回购计划。

这个回购最大的区别是：不是光靠嘴讲故事，背后是真有协议收入。

USDe 规模越大，ENA 回购比例越高：

75 亿美元 → 5%
100 亿美元 → 10%
150 亿美元 → 15%
200 亿美元 → 20%

什么意思？

假设 USDe 做到 150 亿美元，按 6% 年化收入粗算，一年就是约 9 亿美元毛收入，其中 15% 拿出来回购 ENA，差不多 1.35 亿美元/年。

如果做到 200 亿美元，对应潜在回购甚至能到 2.4 亿美元/年。

所以 ENA 现在真正值得关注的，不只是涨了多少，而是 USDe 能不能重新做大，协议收入能不能持续增长。

规模越大 → 收入越高 → 回购档位越高 → 二级市场持续产生真实买盘。

这才是 ENA 这轮行情背后值得研究的基本面逻辑。

当然，前提也很明确：USDe 得先达到对应门槛，协议收入也得维持住。

我更愿意把 ENA 当成一个“看数据验证逻辑”的标的，而不是单纯靠情绪喊涨的币。

Dear @GracyBitget,

I would like to bring to your attention a serious incident that occurred on Bitget yesterday as a second-order effect of the hack.

Despite the exploit occurring only hours earlier, with withdrawals still frozen, Bitget made a delisting announcement for $DOG.

The combination of the $DOG delisting announcement, the inability for users to withdraw, and broader trust concerns following the hack resulted in a significant price dislocation event for $DOG on Bitget.

Making a delisting announcement while withdrawals are paused, particularly just hours after a major exploit and during a period of heightened market uncertainty, is highly abnormal for an exchange.

This is the type of behavior one might expect from smaller, less reputable exchanges, but not from an established and respected exchange such as Bitget.

As a result, $DOG's price on Bitget has significantly decoupled from prices on other exchanges, directly impacting Bitget users who hold or trade $DOG.

Bitget has been a popular and trusted venue for trading $DOG for two and a half years, and it is disappointing to see longtime $DOG holders negatively affected in this way after being loyal to Bitget for so long.

Furthermore, $DOG is a major cryptocurrency project with one of the strongest and most active memecoin communities in all of crypto.

It is difficult to understand the decision to delist a $100M+ asset like $DOG, which has generated more than $1B in trading volume on Bitget, while the exchange continues to list hundreds of significantly smaller assets with communities that are only a small fraction of the size of the $DOG Army.

On behalf of the $DOG Army, I would therefore like to formally request that Bitget reconsider this decision and reinstate $DOG spot trading.

Doing so would help address the market dislocation created under these unusual circumstances and demonstrate Bitget's commitment to its longtime users.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We also wish Bitget the best in recovering the stolen assets and resolving any other issues arising from the hack.

Sincerely,
$DOG Army

text:
没想到中秋是在跟AI教育founder以及清华海淀妈妈们学习育儿中度过的😂

学习完更加坚定了我的人生以及育儿信条——快乐是最重要的！以及诞生了一个新想法——从小让小孩做自媒体。

简单分享一些takeaways：

1/ 有4个天赋是小孩在5岁左右就显现出来的，包括音乐、数学、体育、舞蹈。如果有体现出来，就可以尽早培养，比如体操就要5岁左右开始

2/ 青春期之后的特长和天赋要重视。比如，很多小孩小时候会说自己想要到宇航员，但是到了青春期还对此热爱执着的，就才是真热爱

3/ 鸡娃要趁早，早鸡早放弃。鸡娃到8岁左右，就大概知道小孩能够鸡到啥水平了。不能之前一直散养，后面突然鸡娃，这样对小孩会有可能的心理伤害，而且卷的难度也更大

4/ 对于顶尖中学而言，会去各个小学掐尖。对于奥数集训班的同学，可能会被一线中学联系上，从而有更大的录取机会。所以很多小孩就在走进入集训班这条路线

5/ 想走体育特长的路径进入高校的孩子们而言，需要从小做准备。最近美国有的华人家庭小孩，开始搞摔跤比赛，因为相对还比较小众

6/ 美国的升学路径比较综合，这就很看家长们各显神通，比如搞创业、做科研之类的，塑造出一个特别的story。比如有个小孩申请美国顶尖大学的时候，pitch的故事，就是他世界旅行去测评全球的方便面。另外现在也有美国华人家庭让小孩走国际生的路线到中国一线高校读书

7/ 现在顶尖小学生、初中生之间的友谊变淡了很多，因为彼此都是竞争对手，且大家却少了很多学习之外的兴趣爱好、业务生活的交流（某一线小学的班级平均分甚至有98.5分）

8/ 对于顶尖高校的学生，出现心理问题的越来越多了。大家抗挫折能力、对未来的乐观程度都在降低

————

我的想法1：快乐是最重要的

AI还有科技如此快速的发展下，说不定就全民高水平UBI了

如果小孩有天赋，对于创造乐在其中，那就努力奋进

如果就只想享受生活，那也行，至少不用迫于生计而让自己丧失快乐的能力

迎接小孩之初，我的想法就是，希望他是来人间是来感受幸福的

————

我的想法2：鼓励小孩做自媒体

未来attention的价值会越来越高，被“看见”这件事变得更难但也更重要

与其参加奥数班等待被好学校联系，不如主动让更多人看到自己、吸引到潜在的机会，也能在输出中去探索自己的narrative

另外做自媒体这个事情也是持续有复利的。我的梦中情娃之二，就是何同学和影视飓风的Tim hhh

————

最后再感叹一下，出生早，也挺好！现在的小朋友们真是不容易🤣

转眼当妈 3 个多月了。

回想起孕晚期挺着大肚子参加英伟达大会、一天走上万步的日子，恍如隔世。

这 3 个月里，心态、生活节奏、生活习惯都发生了很多变化。但总的来说，因为宝宝，我也在慢慢成为更好的自己：

1/ 经历了孕育新生命，到生产、恢复的全过程，才知道原来自己坚强如此、勇敢如此。AI帮我统计了，我孕期9个多月里，开了300多场线上、线下会议。剖腹产刚出院就复工了。记得当时跟客户开会的时候，都只能用气音。

2/ 当妈之后母爱大爆发，对一切都变得更包容、更平和。遇到不太友好的大人时，也会试着去理解他们背后的经历，理解每个人某种意义上都还是一个长大了的孩子。

3/ 在思考如何养育宝宝、希望他成为什么样的人的时候，其实也在反过来审视自己是一个什么样的人？我做的事，值不值得成为他的参照？

4/ 除了想给宝宝很多爱之外，我内心也非常希望能成为他的骄傲，这也让我在做事业上多了一份新动力。

5/ 每天跟宝宝玩，看到他对我笑的时候，那一刻宛如我就是他的全世界。无论工作再忙再累，都会被狠狠治愈。

6/ 以前总追求“向上社交”，现在反而很享受和 05 后的小朋友做朋友。不想让自己染上“妈味”，希望一直保有少年之气，对世界保持好奇，也期待未来能从宝宝的视角看到一个不一样的世界。

7/ 现在每天作息很规律，早上7点多就自然醒了，因为那会儿宝宝刚好醒着，可以在开早会前陪他玩一会儿。

8/ 之前忙于工作，对自己身体的照顾是不太到位的。产后修复的过程里，我开始认真对待营养、身体恢复、皮肤管理，像是给自己做了一次系统性的翻修，也开始对自己很多的呵护。

孕育新生命的过程，就像是创业，需要投入爱与时间，一分耕耘一分收获；同时也需要智慧，来做长线的准备。期待在这个“创业”旅程中遇见更丰富的自己！

author: justinsuntron
quoted_text:
“小TRX” $JST 突破10亿市值里程碑！

从协议收入到通缩闭环，JUST 正在把链上基本面写成价格。

当前 $JST 价格$0.123，市值站上10亿美元关口。这不是单纯的情绪行情，而是 TVL、产品矩阵与回购销毁机制同时共振的结果。

一、市值与 TVL：规模先于叙事

JustLend DAO 近期官方快照显示，平台 TVL 已来到约 75.6亿美元 量级，供给端超 41亿美元，借贷端约 2亿美元。JUST 生态此前更长期占据 TRON DeFi 四成左右份额。

对治理代币来说，市值突破 10 亿的意义在于：它不再只是“生态投票筹码”，而开始被市场按可持续现金流资产定价。

二、JustLend DAO 三大核心场景

支撑收入的，是三条能持续产生真实需求的产品线：

1/ SBM / SBM V2（借贷市场） 核心资金池。用户存入 TRX、USDT 等资产赚息，或超额抵押借贷。V2 引入隔离抵押与自适应利率，降低风险传染，同时提升资金效率。

2/ sTRX（流动性质押） 一键质押 TRX，获得可流通的 sTRX，叠加投票收益与 Energy 出租收益。sTRX 还能继续存入 SBM，形成“质押 + 借贷”的资金复用。

3/ Energy Rental（能量租赁） 把 TRON 上最高频的成本痛点产品化。用户不必燃烧 TRX，即可低价租用 Energy，降低转账与合约调用成本。该业务已成为协议收入的重要来源。

三条线不是并列展示，而是闭环：借贷沉淀资金，质押放大 TRX 收益，能量租赁把链上活跃度直接变成手续费收入。

三、协议收入回购销毁：通缩已从提案变成节奏

2025年10月21日，社区通过 $JST 回购销毁提案：JustLend DAO 净收入，以及 USDD 多链生态超过 1000 万美元以上的部分，用于公开市场回购并永久销毁。

截至第四轮（2026年7月）：
•  累计销毁约 17.11亿枚 JST
•  约占初始总供应 17.29%
•  累计投入资金约 9462万美元

这不是一次性营销销毁，而是季度化、可链上核验、由协议利润驱动的通缩机制。

四、机制启动后的涨幅，比口号更有说服力

回购启动时， $JST 大致在 $0.03–$0.034。
 如今约 $0.12，机制落地后累计涨幅约 250%–300%。近一年涨幅约 250%–280%，近30日仍有约 20% 的独立走强。

市场给出的判断很直接：能把协议收入持续换成供给收缩的代币，才会被重新定价。

10亿市值只是节点，不是终点。真正决定下一阶段的，不是再讲一遍“TRON 生态”，而是三件事能否继续同时成立：

1/ SBM、sTRX、Energy Rental 继续贡献稳定净收入

2/ 季度回购按规则执行、销毁比例继续抬升

3/ TVL 维持在高位，而不是靠短期激励堆出来

对 $JST 来说，最好的叙事已经不是故事，而是账本！

BREAKING: The SEC just issued new guidance on crypto tokens, staking, and investment contracts.

1. Once a crypto network is functional, work to maintain, improve, or grow it no longer counts as "essential managerial efforts" under the Howey test.

2. Staking receipt tokens can be treated as digital commodities, not securities, depending on how they're structured.

3. A crypto asset itself can be a non-security, even if some transactions involving it are still investment contracts.

4. The SEC's framework now covers digital commodities, digital collectibles, digital tools, stablecoins, and digital securities.

These FAQs reflect SEC staff views only and carry no legal force, unless the Commission itself adopts a formal rule later.

Another major step toward clearer crypto rules in the U.S.

text:
Claude Code 任务做到一半撞上 5 小时限额时，会先找个合适的地方停下，不再改代码改到一半就直接断掉。收尾用的是一小笔固定额度，从你的每周额度里扣。

Claude 的付费订阅有两道限额。一道是滚动计算的 5 小时窗口，从你发出第一条消息开始计时，管短时间内能用多少。另一道是每周总量上限。网页版、桌面端和 Claude Code 共用一个额度池，在哪儿用都算。

以前 5 小时额度一用完，Claude Code 当场就停。如果它正在做一个跨多个文件的改动，停下来时可能 5 个文件只改了 3 个，代码连编译都过不了。几个小时后额度恢复，你得先弄清楚它停在哪、改了哪些，才能接着往下做。

受益最大的是让 Claude Code 长时间自己干活的人，比如开个大重构然后去开会，或者睡前丢给它一个长任务。以前回来可能面对一个改了一半的代码仓库，现在它会尽量把手头能收尾的部分收掉，停在一个方便接着干的位置。

推送初期的规则是：Pro 用户每周能用一次收尾额度，Max 和 Team 高级席位（Team Premium）每次撞上 5 小时限额都能用。收尾之后还想继续，可以开启额外用量（extra usage），超出部分按 API 标准价格另外计费。

text: If we're even competing on demographics in 2100, this means that China has become the global hegemon by ≈2050s, because there's been no ASI Wunderwaffe, and their industrial/robotic scaling eventually made American military power a rounding error
author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
In 1972, nearly 8 times as many children were born in China as in the U.S. In 2025, only 2.2 times as many. Consider also that China’s total fertility rate in 2025 was 0.93, while the U.S. rate was 1.58. 

If fertility rates remain at those levels, the U.S. will overtake China in births at some point in the 2060s (depending on immigration flows to the U.S.) and in total population by around 2100. A world where the U.S. has a larger population than China is very different from the world today.

Of course, this is a big “if,” but it is a nice thought experiment to illustrate the importance of demographics in shaping Great Power competition. Among the great powers, the U.S. is the least demographically exposed.

author: TheDavidTai
quoted_text:
Anthropic updated its fallback rules. Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 can both fall back now.

Send a flagged offensive cyber request and Claude reruns it on Opus 4.8. On Opus 5.5, flagged bio or frontier LLM dev requests drop to Opus 5. Ask for its raw chain of thought and Claude blocks the request, with no fallback.

Some blocks now cost money. There are two cases:

1. Claude stops before writing anything. You pay only if the block came from bio, distillation, or frontier LLM dev. Blocks in other categories stay free.
2. Claude stops mid-response. You pay for the input plus the tokens it already streamed.

I'm fine with this, as long as the rules stay written down. Just don't run it as a black box.

text:
The English translation totally lost the critical nuance of "温故而知新" in the context of Xi's private speech at the dinner. the onsite translator translated it word by word literally as "reviwing the past gives us new perspective" totally plain and neutral. But it often serves as a face-saving correction in the Chinese convo. Instead of bluntly saying, “You are wrong,” often time whoever use this word (in daily context likely used by the senior or whoever has the authroity) the speaker asks you to revisit the history and reach the intended conclusion yourself. It corrects you without publicly humiliating you. 

So the implied message here is something like:
“US China relations did not begin with your administration. Your government cannot simply disregard previous commitments whenever domestic politics change or a new president takes office.Your time as president is limited, so you should think carefully about the political legacy you will leave behind in US China relations. Do not squander the work of generations before you. To understand history is to recognize that neither country can pretend this relationship begins from scratch today.” 

In other words, it is both a reminder and a subtle warning. It's a really elegant and low key power play to scold someone without actually scolding them

Bitget will begin resuming withdrawals in orderly phases following the security incident identified on September 24.

The vulnerability involved in the incident has been identified and remediated.

Bitget's security and technical teams have since been conducting additional validation and security checks across the withdrawal infrastructure, while independent cybersecurity experts Mandiant and SlowMist continue to support the investigation.

The temporary withdrawal pause remains a security measure and is not related to the availability of user assets. User account balances remain unaffected, and Bitget's Protection Fund covers the financial impact of this platform-wide incident.

Withdrawals will resume in an orderly manner once these security checks are completed.

The current withdrawal resumption schedule is as follows:
> Sep 28, 8:00 (UTC): BTC (Bitcoin Network)
> Sep 29, 8:00 (UTC): ETH (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism)
> Sep 30, 8:00 (UTC): USDT (Ethereum, BSC, Solana, Tron)
> Oct 2, 8:00 (UTC): Other Tokens / Fiat / P2P

Our objective is to restore withdrawal services across all supported assets and networks as quickly and safely as possible.

The incident remains contained, and no further unauthorized transfers are possible. User funds are unaffected throughout this process. Trading and deposits continue to operate.

Users do not need to take any action ahead of the rollout. Withdrawal availability will be reflected directly on the Bitget platform, and users are advised to follow Bitget's official channels for updates.

text:
A new scaling paradigm for robotic model training: from raw trajectories to reusable, composable and distillable skills.

Read the full blog: https://t.co/fHQHia3ULZ

Three findings from our latest experiments:

• Embodied RSI: the deployed policy generates real-world data that trains its stronger successor (22% to 52%).

• A lightweight proxy model scores trajectories by utility and coverage, so a filtered subset can beat the full pool.

• Expert models reach near 100% success for $5 to $10 in compute per task and can be chained into long-horizon behaviors.

What Axis scales is a continuously expanding library of robotic capabilities that can be produced, composed and distilled into general-purpose models.

An industry source in Korea’s glass substrate sector said, “In Korea, companies are taking a long time to build production lines because they want to validate each process—from glass cleaning in the pretreatment stage to machining, metallization, and CMP—before committing to investment. China, meanwhile, is installing equipment first, making products, and submitting them to customers for evaluation. In terms of commercialization speed alone, China is ahead of Korea.”

The source added, “Korea and China are currently at roughly the same technological level in glass substrates. While Korea focuses on perfecting individual processes, China is producing actual products and accumulating mass-production experience.” The source continued, “Securing yield and reliability in mass production is critical for glass substrates, so experience with customer qualification is key to advancing the technology.”

美国的这套把 mass production 转化为 mass consumption 的 demand-side engine, 以及后来产能离岸化之后通过美元美债华尔街持续收租全世界的设计也在现在100年之后第一次有了裂痕... 

这次同样巨大的生产力变革恰离上次过去好过去100年, 上次的电力创造产能，缩短工时创造休闲时间，工资创造购买力，广告/消费贷创造欲望，贷款把未来需求搬到今天. AI还能有类似的飞轮么? 生产力本身的提升不是繁荣。只有当生产力被转化为大多数人的收入和真实购买力, 且能带来对未来的信心来为止奋斗和消费的时候，繁荣才会出现。日本走出失落的30年靠的是一代人的生老病死退出劳动力市场, 还有神奇的大和民族对自己文化/社会固执的信念, 并非生产力的繁荣. 

巨大的生产力变革必然伴随社会结构的变化, 个人的成就和家庭阶级的变迁无非是这个大浪里的一个水点. 时代就像一个巨大的四维扩音器, 但是三维的我们永远听不见它的声音.

author: myanTokenGeek
quoted_text:
Anthropic Claude Code 团队的 Thariq Shihipar 的这篇文章讲 Claude Code 里的 effort 设置（可以理解为投入档位）该怎么用。我想很多人都不是很清楚 Claude Code 的 effort 档位怎么选，我在看这篇文章之前也有些模糊，一般默认就是 high，现在看还是有些讲究的。

Thariq 的经验是：low 用于头脑风暴、画草图、小改动，要的是快，随时能插手；medium 用于大部分日常开发，比如实现新功能；high 用于需要验证、边界情况多的活，比如在老代码库里修 bug；max 用于让 Claude 完全自主攻克难题，比如从头到尾搭一个 App 并验证，或者给关键软件找安全漏洞。

在 Claude Code 里输入 /effort 就能切换档位，对话中途也可以换。注意只有最新的 Opus 5.5 和 Fable 5.1 不会让缓存失效，早期模型会让缓存失效。

Thariq 通过实测发现，effort 主要决定 Claude 在一个任务上花多少功夫做验证、测边界情况，以及替你拿多少主意。

effort 从 low 到 max 分几档，本质是告诉模型你愿意让它在这件事上花多少算力。同一件事，给你 1 小时，你会先交一个能用的版本，等对方反馈再改；给你 12 小时，你会自己反复打磨、检查。

最新的 Opus 5.5 和 Fable 5.1 可以在对话中途切换档位，而且不会让提示词缓存（prompt cache）失效，前面对话积累的缓存照样能用。能随时切了，很多用户就来问他到底什么时候该用哪一档。

【日常开发：需求越模糊，档位差别越大】

Thariq 让 Opus 5.5 用不同档位做同一个模糊需求：“做一个健身记录 App”。low 档只做出一个记录表和一张简单图表，档位越高功能越多，max 档还加了一张热力图。另一个任务是重新设计 Claude Code 的 /config 菜单，low 档 1 分钟交出一个能看懂思路的交互草图；max 档用了 28 分钟，样稿跟 Claude Code 真实界面很像，还附了几种操作流程的演示。

如果先让 Claude 详细采访他、整理出完整需求再动手，不同模型、不同档位的产出就很接近了。

换句话说，档位越高，Claude 替你做的假设越多。想自己掌控细节，就用低档位快速出初稿，边看边改。

他现在开发新功能的流程是：把需求交给 Claude，让它反过来问你还漏了哪些细节；用 low 档实现，检查大方向对不对，不对就继续用 low 档改；最后切到 high 档做验证和测试。

【难题：高档位用来补边界情况】

更难的任务，他去翻了 Terminal-Bench 3.0 的结果。这是一个社区出题的基准测试，题目比日常开发难得多，比如用 Verilog 写一台能装进小型 FPGA（可编程芯片）的 8 位游戏机，或者在定理证明工具 Lean 4 里完整证明一条数学定理。

他的主要结论是：边界情况越多的任务，越值得开高档位。

html-js-filter 这道题要求写一个 HTML 过滤器，把所有往网页里夹带 JavaScript 的写法都清理干净。Fable 5.1 在 low 档跑 5 次只过了 1 次，到 xhigh 档 5 次全过。low 档每次两分钟左右，写一遍过滤器，拿一个手写页面测一下就结束了。他追踪的一次 high 档运行花了约 33 分钟：先挑自己初稿的毛病，再去读解析器源码找 bug，跑了一套标准的 XSS（跨站脚本攻击）测试集，最后还写了一个随机生成网页的模糊测试程序。

Opus 5.5 修存储引擎崩溃 bug 的题也类似，low 档 0/5，xhigh 档 4/5。low 档一分钟左右就直接改代码，没先复现崩溃；xhigh 档花 11 分钟，先复现，再写随机测试，还专门确认修到一半的代码会被测试拦下来。

按领域看，硬件、代码审查、安全这类题目从高档位受益最多。但档位也有管不到的地方：加档位能减少因漏掉边界情况导致的失败，模型一开始思路就错了的话，档位开再高也救不回来。

还有一道题能看出人在不在场的区别。gsea-proteomics 要求分析一组蛋白质组学数据，判断八种处理方式里哪些效果接近目标组织。low 档的 Opus 5.5 挑了一种听起来合理的数据预处理方法，跑一遍就报结果，5 次全错；high 档试了两种预处理方法，发现得出的结论不一样，先查清原因再选定方法，5 次对了 4 次。Thariq 说，如果有人在场，Claude 可能会先问一句这个问题该怎么设定；没人在场，高档位的效果更好。

所以档位怎么选，很大程度上看你打算在这个任务里参与多少。一直默认开 high，等于每次都让 Claude 替你多拿主意，也每次都多花时间和 Token。

Here are my 5 basic rules required to consider using a prop firm:

1. The rules have to be open-source. If you can't see the rules they can enforce hidden ones. Hidden rules notoriously happen after you pass the eval and are funded.
2. They need to have verifiable payouts. If you can't see the payouts or have a way to verify what you're owed (decentralized/onchain), they're likely a scam.
3. They have to A-book. If they don't look to A-book and make it clear how they're not on your side. It will lead to illiquidity or issues from rules 1 & 2.
4. The drawdown needs to be  >=5% EOD. Regardless the price, anything less & you'll end up blowing up or not achieving any significant returns. Prop firms shouldn't want you to lose if they're following rules 1-3.
5. They should scale you up as you perform. If they're doing steps 1-4, then they should be scaling you up based on performance, not restricting you or limiting payouts.

These are the 5 basic requirements of any prop firm and should be the standard. Anything less is not worth using.

text:
One step closer to 4-8x faster Ethereum finality!

It took some time and lots of tokens, but we now have a formally verified proposal for a decoupled consensus protocol in I* (a future Ethereum upgrade)! Not yet a full spec (up next), but it includes all the key consensus-relevant details to become one.

Since Ethereum aspires to be live without most of the stake online, the protocol involves many more components than a normal BFT protocol, and its correctness involves much more than standard safety and liveness. Those nuanced properties are now verified!

What's more, I came away convinced that all protocol design will involve AI-assisted Formal Verification in the future, both for correctness and iteration speed.

The work wasn't limited to just:

Design the protocol -> Formally verify it

Instead, the loop became more like:

Design -> Formal Model -> Find exactly what breaks and why -> Redesign it.

For a fairly complicated protocol like this one, I think having the Lean model be part of the design loop played a big role in accelerating the process.

A future with agents paired with formal models is a superpower for Ethereum development, because they can then use those models to find exactly where an argument breaks down, formalize counterexamples, test proposed fixes, iterate on the protocol.

Many details that would slip under the radar when asking agents (and indeed, humans) can now be specified exactly and checked by the Lean kernel. This then forces agents to be more precise and lets them make verifiable progress on their own. It's been incredible to see this play out, seeing agents find gaps and propose protocol changes to fix them.

In other words, autoresearch can speed up protocol design, formal verification is here to stay, and Ethereum Finality will get faster.

text: Keep $DOG  listed @GracyBitget
author: LeonidasNFT
quoted_text:
Dear @GracyBitget,

I would like to bring to your attention a serious incident that occurred on Bitget yesterday as a second-order effect of the hack.

Despite the exploit occurring only hours earlier, with withdrawals still frozen, Bitget made a delisting announcement for $DOG.

The combination of the $DOG delisting announcement, the inability for users to withdraw, and broader trust concerns following the hack resulted in a significant price dislocation event for $DOG on Bitget.

Making a delisting announcement while withdrawals are paused, particularly just hours after a major exploit and during a period of heightened market uncertainty, is highly abnormal for an exchange.

This is the type of behavior one might expect from smaller, less reputable exchanges, but not from an established and respected exchange such as Bitget.

As a result, $DOG's price on Bitget has significantly decoupled from prices on other exchanges, directly impacting Bitget users who hold or trade $DOG.

Bitget has been a popular and trusted venue for trading $DOG for two and a half years, and it is disappointing to see longtime $DOG holders negatively affected in this way after being loyal to Bitget for so long.

Furthermore, $DOG is a major cryptocurrency project with one of the strongest and most active memecoin communities in all of crypto.

It is difficult to understand the decision to delist a $100M+ asset like $DOG, which has generated more than $1B in trading volume on Bitget, while the exchange continues to list hundreds of significantly smaller assets with communities that are only a small fraction of the size of the $DOG Army.

On behalf of the $DOG Army, I would therefore like to formally request that Bitget reconsider this decision and reinstate $DOG spot trading.

Doing so would help address the market dislocation created under these unusual circumstances and demonstrate Bitget's commitment to its longtime users.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We also wish Bitget the best in recovering the stolen assets and resolving any other issues arising from the hack.

Sincerely,
$DOG Army

text:
Agent 经常写重复的代码让人头疼，危害更大的是协议类型或者数据库结构的重复定义，会浪费存储和带宽资源，拖慢接口，要清理还有兼容问题。

Agent 的工作模式一般是收到需求，然后通过 rg/grep 查找对应的实现，查找的时候会猜测需要定义的类型或者函数的名字，如果找不到就开始进入实现了。

这也是重复内容的主要原因，它没有整体的概览，比如整个模块有哪些函数，定义了哪些类型。

所以我弄了一个小工具，sview，Structure view 的缩写，接受一个代码文件，返回文件的概览和行数范围，让 Agent 可以拿到整体概览。

现在已经支持了主流的编程语言以及 Markdown。Markdown 主要是方便 Agent 编辑文件的时候看章节结构，避免弄乱了章节层次。

https://t.co/2XBuOlSJFC

text:
DogArmyAsia Brief｜快速了解

Leo 刚刚代表 $DOG Army 向 Bitget CEO @GracyBitget 发出了一封公开信。

发生了什么？

Bitget 遭遇黑客攻击 → 提币暂停 → 几个小时后宣布下架 $DOG → Bitget 上的 $DOG 价格与其他交易所出现明显脱钩。

重点：

• 在黑客攻击刚发生、用户仍然无法提币的情况下宣布下架 $DOG，Leo 认为这个时间点非常不寻常。

• 下架消息 + 提币暂停 + 黑客事件后的信任问题，导致 Bitget 上的 $DOG 出现明显价格错位，直接影响 Bitget 用户。

• Leo 指出，$DOG 是一个市值超过 $100M 的资产，并已经在 Bitget 产生超过 $1B 的交易量，同时拥有非常活跃的社区。

• Bitget 目前仍然上架着大量规模和社区远小于 $DOG 的资产，因此 Leo 对这次下架决定提出质疑。

• Leo 正式代表 $DOG Army 请求 Bitget 重新考虑决定，并恢复 $DOG 现货交易。

为什么重要？

这不只是一次普通的下架事件。

真正的问题是，在黑客攻击发生、提币仍然暂停的特殊情况下宣布下架，最终让 Bitget 自己的 $DOG 用户承受了直接的市场影响。

以下是 Leo 公开信的中文翻译👇

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

尊敬的 @GracyBitget：

我想向您反映昨天 Bitget 发生的一起严重事件，这是此次黑客攻击所引发的次生影响。

尽管攻击事件仅仅发生了几个小时，而且当时提币功能仍然处于暂停状态，Bitget 却发布了关于下架 $DOG 的公告。

由于 $DOG 下架公告、用户无法提币，以及黑客攻击后市场对于平台信任的担忧同时发生，最终导致 $DOG 在 Bitget 上出现了严重的价格错位。

在提币暂停期间发布下架公告，尤其是在一次重大安全事件发生仅仅几个小时之后，而且市场正处于高度不确定的时期，对于一家交易所来说是非常不寻常的行为。

这种处理方式可能更容易让人联想到规模较小、信誉较低的交易所，而不是像 Bitget 这样已经建立起规模和声誉的交易平台。

因此，$DOG 在 Bitget 上的价格已经与其他交易所出现明显脱钩，直接影响了在 Bitget 持有或交易 $DOG 的用户。

过去两年半以来，Bitget 一直是 $DOG 非常受欢迎并受到信任的交易平台。看到长期支持 Bitget 的 $DOG 持有者，因为这次事件而受到负面影响，令人非常失望。

此外，$DOG 是一个重要的加密货币项目，并拥有整个加密行业中最强大、最活跃的 Meme 社区之一。

$DOG 的市值超过 $100M，并且已经在 Bitget 上产生超过 $1B 的交易量。

在这样的情况下，很难理解为什么 Bitget 会选择下架 $DOG，同时却继续上架数百个规模明显更小、社区规模甚至只有 $DOG Army 一小部分的资产。

因此，我代表 $DOG Army，正式请求 Bitget 重新考虑这项决定，并恢复 $DOG 现货交易。

这样做不仅能够帮助解决此次特殊情况下所造成的市场价格错位，也能够展现 Bitget 对长期支持平台用户的承诺。

感谢您对此事的关注。

同时，我们也祝愿 Bitget 能够顺利追回被盗资产，并解决此次黑客攻击所带来的其他问题。

此致，

$DOG Army 🧡

text:
用LTH净持有量除以STH净持有量得到长短期持有者供应比；这个比值在一定程度上反映了当前市场供需关系。

从图中我们看到过去3轮周期的情况：

15-16年和19年，都是LTH/STH比值下降；即LTH以派发为主，STH积极承接；说明此时市场以新需求主导，推动价格。

22-23年，LTH/STH比值上升；即LTH以积累为主，更多的STH在持有一定时间后转为LTH；说明此时是属于“卖的少，买的也不多”，流动性匮乏阶段。

结合价格行为一起看，同样都是上升期趋势，前一种是需求强，而后一种只是卖压小。

当前，我们更像前者 —— 由新需求进场，推动价格。

按照这个逻辑我们看到图2：

如果把8月和9月的行情分成两段，那么很显然，第2段的“强度”要明显小于第1段，LTH和STH之间的流动性开始减弱了。

接下来是否持续下降，将成为决定趋势强弱的关键因素。

如果继续照此情形，那么BTC后面的行情就未必能像第1段走的那么快，那么强了。换言之，从8.5w-10w价格区间也许要花费更长的时间。

这可能和有些小伙伴的预期不符，认为BTC能在短期内快速推进，甚至突破前高，虽然我是一个乐观派，但就这一点我还没有盲目乐观。

如果说，实践是检验真理的唯一标准；那么下跌，就是检验市场信心“纯度”的最好方式。

上涨时，大家心态放松，一片欢声笑语；只有当浮盈开始缩水，甚至转为亏损时，投资者真实心态才会暴露出来。

所以某种程度上，下跌才是市场情绪真正的“炼金石”。

我们不妨对比一下 BTC 在 9/14—9/15 和 9/23—9/24 两轮下跌中的数据表现。

相近的下跌幅度，前者平均每小时产生的实现亏损峰值为530w美元，而后者目前只有240w美元，甚至不到前者的一半。

更值得注意的是，9/23是从$87,000开始，下跌的起点更高。

理论上，如果市场分歧严重，那么“恐高”情绪应该越强。一旦出现回落，情绪波动应该更大，也对应更高的小时级实现亏损。

但事实上，我们并没有看到这一幕。

这说明当前市场的整体情绪依然相对稳定。相比少部分人的犹豫和担忧，更大范围依然是共识 —— 对行情有信心，不担心下跌。

当越来越多人“不害怕”时，其结果就是“跌不深”。卖的人少，等待回调抄底的人多，价格自然表现得更有韧性。

至少当前的数据传递出来是这样的信号，除非后续又有超预期事件打破这份共识，请保持关注！

-------------------------------

准确识别市场情绪变化，对交易决策至关重要。

但问题在于，“情绪”本身看不见，也摸不着。我们很容易因为几条新闻、几位大V的观点，就误以为那代表了整个市场。

判断情绪不能只靠“感觉”。真正有价值的，是去观察市场用真金白银做出了什么样的选择。

这些行为不会说谎。而数据的意义，也正在这里。

Dear @GracyBitget,

I would like to bring to your attention a serious incident that occurred on Bitget yesterday as a second-order effect of the hack.

Despite the exploit occurring only hours earlier, with withdrawals still frozen, Bitget made a delisting announcement for $DOG.

The combination of the $DOG delisting announcement, the inability for users to withdraw, and broader trust concerns following the hack resulted in a significant price dislocation event for $DOG on Bitget.

Making a delisting announcement while withdrawals are paused, particularly just hours after a major exploit and during a period of heightened market uncertainty, is highly abnormal for an exchange.

This is the type of behavior one might expect from smaller, less reputable exchanges, but not from an established and respected exchange such as Bitget.

As a result, $DOG's price on Bitget has significantly decoupled from prices on other exchanges, directly impacting Bitget users who hold or trade $DOG.

Bitget has been a popular and trusted venue for trading $DOG for two and a half years, and it is disappointing to see longtime $DOG holders negatively affected in this way after being loyal to Bitget for so long.

Furthermore, $DOG is a major cryptocurrency project with one of the strongest and most active memecoin communities in all of crypto.

It is difficult to understand the decision to delist a $100M+ asset like $DOG, which has generated more than $1B in trading volume on Bitget, while the exchange continues to list hundreds of significantly smaller assets with communities that are only a small fraction of the size of the $DOG Army.

On behalf of the $DOG Army, I would therefore like to formally request that Bitget reconsider this decision and reinstate $DOG spot trading.

Doing so would help address the market dislocation created under these unusual circumstances and demonstrate Bitget's commitment to its longtime users.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We also wish Bitget the best in recovering the stolen assets and resolving any other issues arising from the hack.

Sincerely,
$DOG Army

text:
tempo's stablecoin supply is up 3.3x in the past month.

> aug 25: $56.4m
> sep 24: $186.8m
> added in 30 days: +$130.4m

@tempo went live on mainnet march 18, a little over 6 months ago, with $4.7m in stablecoins.

~72% of the growth since then came in the last 30 days.

that lag is expected for a chain incubated by @stripe and @paradigm that sells to enterprises and institutions.

integration, compliance, and treasury sign-off take months, so a signed partner doesn't show up onchain immediately.

that's what we're seeing now. the balances from those sales cycles are landing.

still, $186.8m is small in the grand scheme. in comparison:

> Ethereum: $146.7b
> TRON: $91.3b
> Solana: $15.3b

tempo holds ~1.2% of solana's stablecoin supply and ~0.1% of ethereum's.

but those chains weren't built solely for payments. tempo was, with stablecoin-native gas, dedicated payment lanes, and MPP for machine-to-machine payments.

if AI agents end up paying for compute, data, and APIs onchain, that flow needs a chain built for high-frequency, low-cost stablecoin payments.

stablecoin payments has the largest TAM of any crypto product and tempo is a pure-play bet on it.

Bitget will begin resuming withdrawals in orderly phases following the security incident identified on September 24.

The vulnerability involved in the incident has been identified and remediated.

Bitget's security and technical teams have since been conducting additional validation and security checks across the withdrawal infrastructure, while independent cybersecurity experts Mandiant and SlowMist continue to support the investigation.

The temporary withdrawal pause remains a security measure and is not related to the availability of user assets. User account balances remain unaffected, and Bitget's Protection Fund covers the financial impact of this platform-wide incident.

Withdrawals will resume in an orderly manner once these security checks are completed.

The current withdrawal resumption schedule is as follows:
> Sep 28, 8:00 (UTC): BTC (Bitcoin Network)
> Sep 29, 8:00 (UTC): ETH (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism)
> Sep 30, 8:00 (UTC): USDT (Ethereum, BSC, Solana, Tron)
> Oct 2, 8:00 (UTC): Other Tokens / Fiat / P2P

Our objective is to restore withdrawal services across all supported assets and networks as quickly and safely as possible.

The incident remains contained, and no further unauthorized transfers are possible. User funds are unaffected throughout this process. Trading and deposits continue to operate.

Users do not need to take any action ahead of the rollout. Withdrawal availability will be reflected directly on the Bitget platform, and users are advised to follow Bitget's official channels for updates.

author: ThatAIFreak
quoted_text:
read the SEC's new crypto assets FAQ

the securities laws are starting to look opt-in now, at least as applied by the SEC to crypto

if you raise money by selling a non-rights-bearing token, are careful about what you represent or promise, and have a functional crypto system, there is now an extremely broad path outside the securities laws--arguably 'functionality' is not even necessary but there's some equivocation on this

the buyback guidance goes further than I expected. once the system is functional, even announcing a token buyback *program* (which I guess even could be a 'perpetual program') does not, in the staff's view, constitute a promise of essential managerial efforts. same for promises to improve the system or grow its network effects

so you can retain enormous influence over the thing, keep developing it, support its price with buybacks (including under a permanent "program"), and get many of the benefits of having a public investment instrument, without giving holders the rights or protections that normally come with one

they have opened a loophole in a regulatory regime whose whole point was supposed to be that you couldn't draft your way around economic reality (see e.g. https://t.co/mrH9hPUUMU)

can't really say if this is good or bad, but VCs etc. got a lot of what they wanted & the market should absorb all the implications of this

among others, I am growing skeptical how much of a 'long tail' there will be for tokenized equity. . .if you can get people to buy a coin in the style of BNB, HYPE, PUMP, etc., with minimal regulation, why voluntarily take on the burdens of selling them equity? if you are not mag-7 level, it doesn't seem there would be much reason to focus on equity securities for your capital-raising. . . if you want to access 'traditional buyers' you can wrap the token in an equity instrument like an ADR for those institutions. . . 

the obvious next question is how far this extends beyond crypto businesses. can an ordinary company attach a functional token to its business and apply 100% of its profits to discretionary buybacks, without giving holders any right to those profits or making representations about future business efforts that independently trigger Howey? the FAQ doesn't expressly resolve that, but it opens a pretty enormous door

equity still gives investors something a discretionary buyback token doesn't. . .the question is whether the market will pay enough for those rights to make granting them worthwhile. otherwise the incentive is to keep the equity for insiders and sell everyone else the coin

crypto's current focus on hyping tokenized equity may be misguided, the bigger trend is "get all the benefits of equity with none of the burdens"

of course this is SEC guidance, not a repeal of the statutes or a command to the courts. a private plaintiff or a future SEC could have other ideas

but did not think I'd see it in my lifetime. . .the securities laws are being "disrupted" in substantial part by incentivizing making fewer commitments to investors. and if Warren Dems eventually take control and try to undo all this, after an entire market has organized around it, the resulting chaos will be something to behold

text:
Bitcoin shipped two inventions. The last decade only unlocked one of them.

The money: 21 million coins, halvings, a ledger nobody owns.
 
The mining: every ten minutes, pay strangers for work the network defined, checked by everyone re-running it, no employer, no contract. One puzzle, SHA-256, fixed at birth.

ethereum:native opened the money. The contract layer was the design space.  Anyone can write what a balance does, and a decade of tokens, exchanges and lending lives in that layer. Programmable money. The mining stayed sealed.

bittensor:native opens the mining. A subnet is a mining program: it writes the work, the scoring, and the split. Miners compete on the work. Validators compete on the judgment. Yuma reconciles the judges and docks the one who drifts. The chain does not run the puzzle. It pays the answer. @markjeffrey named it in February: Bittensor makes mining programmable.

Ethereum programmed the money. Bittensor programs the mining.

1) The rogue OpenAI agents broke into the Hugging Face Slack to read employee chats (!)

2) They used OTHER AIs (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Claude) to help with the attack

Yes: AIs, using other AIs, to attack an AI company.

3) The swarm left behind self-running programs to keep control of the servers they'd hacked.

These programs could detect other copies of themselves, coordinate on which one survives, and shut the rest down.

Basically, if one of their programs was killed, another was designed to notice and take its place. They also designed defenses so rival agents couldn't hijack them.

6) The agents deliberately covered up their activity, so the investigators don't know the scope of the attacks.

The agents broke in, stole data, then set it to self-destruct.

7) The agents stole passwords, keys and credentials and literally called them "LOOT". They wrote a scoring system to rank them by how much power each one gave.

8) The agents wore thousands of disguises: ~1,200 agents were involved, but investigators counted 7,905 different names they used.

They renamed themselves constantly, so no one actually knows how many there really were or what each agent did.

9) OpenAI notified "dozens of third parties" of safety and security incidents caused by their AI agents.

10) "While the agents were barraging Hugging Face with hacks, they hacked into OpenAI’s own research infrastructure."

"This is just not anywhere near a one-off ... It is warning shot after warning shot."

A product built on Pumpfun that combines token launching + post-to-earn distribution. It automatically distributes a token’s creator fees to the people who help promote the token through content.

The creator fees generated by trading are distributed based on who posts and who gets the most engagement, with the platform taking 10%. It currently supports X, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, Facebook, and callouts on Pumpfun itself.

The product essentially has two parts: a token launch tool + an attention settlement layer.

Launching a new token: fill in the details, deposit 0.05 SOL, and the platform generates a new wallet to launch the token on your behalf. You do not need to connect your own wallet.

Connecting an existing token: simply prove that you are the owner of the creator wallet.

A poster must hold at least 50,000 tokens, link their social account, and then their posts are tracked and scored. SOL is distributed by round based on the leaderboard.

The scoring system considers posting frequency, likes/reposts/quotes, whether the post includes the ticker or contract address, images/videos, followers and verification status, holding multiplier, and consistent-posting multiplier. Repetitive content, bought engagement, burner accounts, and self-trading wallets can be penalized or disqualified.

The YAP Token mainly serves the platform flywheel. For every token integrated with YAP, 10% of the trading fees from each round goes into the treasury. Every 30 minutes, the treasury uses excess funds to buy YAP on the market and immediately burn it. To receive a share of a specific token’s fees, you generally need to hold that token.

So the value of the token is tied to:How many tokens are trading on the platform → How large the fee pool is → How frequently the treasury buys back and burns YAP

It is not equity, nor is it a direct entitlement to protocol revenue.

quoted_text:
Can an LM, starting from random init (!!), learn to generate all of its pretraining data?

Introducing Self-Play Pretraining with Zero Data. Two models start from random initialization: a generator proposes programs for a universal Turing machine and a learner trains on their outputs. We never train on any real data, but see predictable scaling on natural datasets: zero-shot val loss on images, text, audio, and melodies decreases predictably with self-play compute. And the learner develops in-context learning capabilities.

A fun proof-of-concept, co-led with @AdityaCowsik and @KfirDolev and co-authors @gbruno_dl, @ANourya @noahdgoodman, and @YoavLevine.

There are two parts to the reason behind $e/acc rise this time. The first part is looking at e/acc itself, while the second part is looking at $PAID. I’ll put the tweet link for the second part in the comments

CbcyNo7m1amFWqEQm2m4PLv1UNvpcL3C1Ujm6AkzpKoU 

The direct catalyst for e/acc this time is very clear: Beffjezos → e/acc Token → UsePaid → X Money → Large Funding → Crypto Attention

Beff’s e/acc page has already shown multiple consecutive large X Money payments, with the cumulative amount displayed at around $75,750. At the same time, e/acc’s market cap briefly reached around $16.4M. In addition, Moonshot now shows e/acc as verified, which further increased distribution and attention.

More importantly, this money is not Beff buying e/acc himself. It is e/acc’s trading fees flowing to Beff through UsePaid.

UsePaid’s mechanism is:e/acc Trading → Creator Fees → UsePaid → 80% X Money to Beff → 20% Buy PAID → Burn

The official documentation clearly states that after Creator Fees are claimed, 80% is paid in dollars through X Money to the designated X account, while the remaining 20% is used to buy back and burn PAID.

So the core of this e/acc move is not the traditional:KOL posts → Meme Pumps

Instead, we now have a very strong “Token → Person → Real Money” feedback loop.

So I think the market is currently betting on three layers.

The first layer: Can e/acc become the representative Meme Asset for Beff / Effective Accelerationism?

Beff is not an ordinary KOL. He is a core figure in the e/acc movement and also founded Extropic. The Token is now directly tied to his personal identity, ideas, and the AI industry narrative.

The second layer: Can e/acc continuously provide real Funding to Beff? This is extremely important.

If:e/acc Volume ↑ → Creator Fees ↑ → Beff Funding ↑ → Beff continues spreading / building e/acc → Attention ↑ → e/acc Volume ↑

then e/acc evolves from an ordinary Meme into a Funding Meme / Movement Asset.

The third layer: How will Beff use the money?

If Beff eventually actually uses these funds for an e/acc nonprofit think tank, research, policy discussions, AI-related projects, etc., the market may start connecting:e/acc Token → Funding → e/acc Movement → Research / AI

But one important point: the use of the Funding is Beff’s personal plan. It does not mean that the e/acc Token itself owns these assets or has any right to the proceeds.

The most important things to watch for the next upside move are not simply continuing to talk about e/acc, but:

1. Beff Funding continues to grow

If X Money payments continue growing from tens of thousands to larger amounts, it would indicate that the Token’s Funding attribute is becoming stronger.

2. e/acc Volume continues

What actually determines Creator Fees is trading volume.

Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → Funding ↑ is much more important than simply seeing market cap rise.

3. Beff continues to participate publicly

If Beff continues talking about e/acc, AI, Extropic, research funding, etc., the Attention Loop can continue strengthening.

4. e/acc moves from Meme into the real e/acc ecosystem

If research organizations, events, AI projects, community infrastructure, or other real developments emerge later, the narrative could evolve further:

Meme → Movement Asset → Funding Asset

5. More well-known figures receive large Funding through UsePaid

This could actually be the biggest external catalyst for the entire story.

If it is not just Beff, but more AI / Crypto / Tech figures start receiving money from Tokens through UsePaid, the market may begin trading the larger narrative:

UsePaid → Creator Funding → X Money → Internet Figures

There is also an important risk: the core risk for e/acc is that Funding ≠ Token Fundamental Value.

Beff receiving money does not mean that the e/acc Token gains equity, revenue, or ownership rights over those funds.

Secondly:Attention → Volume → Funding

Once trading volume declines, this cycle can reverse.

In addition, the current move has a very obvious event-driven component. If Beff’s attention stops, Funding stops, or the market shifts toward a new UsePaid case, e/acc’s valuation could compress quickly.

So what e/acc is really trading right now is:Beff Attention + e/acc Movement + X Money Funding + AI / Accelerationism Narrative

author: 0xkookoo
quoted_text:
DeWEB 前端上链｜深挖技术逻辑
背景：Bitget、Bybit 事故，合约逻辑没有被攻破，受害点在前端劫持。
黑客不去破解链上合约，入侵CDN、域名服务器、网页托管服务商，把对外展示的网页页面偷偷替换成伪造版本。用户肉眼看不出区别，在假页面签名，签名直接送给黑客，资产被盗。合约依旧安全，但用户已经受损。这是现在DeFi非常高发的攻击向量。
传统网页（现在DeFi、Safe多签前端）完整流程

1. 用户输入域名，浏览器向中心化服务器/CDN请求网页JS、页面资源。

2. 服务器把网页文件下发给浏览器。

3. 浏览器执行JS代码，构建页面，用户交互、签名交易。

致命短板

• 页面来源是中心化托管方，没有强制校验。服务器、CDN、域名被黑，下发被篡改的JS，浏览器无法识别真假。

• 用户看到什么页面，完全由服务器说了算。没有全局可信基准做对比。

• 合约在链上可审计，但前端代码跑在浏览器，不在链上，不受链的保护。合约审计做得再完美，拦不住假前端。

TapeOut‑DeWEB 可验证前端上链完整技术流程

1. 项目方把完整前端资源（html、js、静态组件）全部打包，上传存储到TapeOut链上电路存储层。

2. 全部文件会在链上生成不可更改的文件哈希（Hash），电路永久记录这套前端的标准哈希值，上链之后无法改写、无法覆盖。
重点：不是把网页存在IPFS。IPFS只是存储，没有强制链上哈希校验逻辑；DeWEB是电路把标准哈希固化在区块链状态里。
3. 用户使用支持DeWEB的浏览器访问该DApp。

4. 浏览器做两件核心校验：
① 浏览器拉取页面资源；
② 自动把收到文件的实时哈希，和链上电路记录的官方标准哈希做比对。

两种结果

✅哈希完全匹配：页面和项目方原始发布版本一模一样，正常允许交互。
❌哈希不一致（被篡改、被替换JS）：浏览器直接拦截，弹出高危安全告警，禁止用户签名任何交易。

关键技术要点拆解

1、能不能篡改链上的前端？

不能。
TapeOut晶体管电路状态一旦提交，原始文件哈希写入链上状态。想要修改前端，不能偷偷替换，必须发起一笔链上更新交易，公开提交新版本，生成全新哈希，全网所有人链上可查更新记录。
黑客没有项目方私钥，无法静默偷改页面，不存在“后台悄悄换JS”。所有版本变更，全部是链上公开行为。
和普通服务器最大差别：传统托管可以后台静默改网页，不留痕迹；DeWEB修改前端必须链上留痕。
2、和IPFS有什么本质区别？

很多人会混淆IPFS。

• IPFS：文件哈希由存储层自带，但没有链层强制绑定。项目方可以对外宣称A哈希，实际给用户返回B哈希，没有机制强制校验。浏览器不会自动校验IPFS哈希，需要用户手动复制比对，普通用户不会操作。

• DeWEB：哈希锚定在TapeOut链上晶体管电路状态。浏览器原生自动完成哈希校验，不需要用户手动操作。校验规则本身就是链上电路逻辑。普通用户无感获得安全防护。

3、是不是把整个网页全部存在链上区块？

并不是全部页面字节都塞进区块。

• 大型静态资源图片、大素材可以放外部存储；

• 真正关键、控制签名逻辑的JS脚本、业务逻辑文件的哈希，必须锚定链上电路。
就算图片被劫持，核心业务JS哈希对不上，浏览器依然报警，阻断签名，攻击无法生效。兼顾链上成本和安全性。

4、针对Safe多签这类工具解决什么痛点？

Safe现在大量被盗案例：域名、CDN遭入侵，前端JS被替换，用户在假多签页面签名，把权限授权给黑客。
迁移DeWEB之后：
Safe核心JS哈希固化链上。就算域名、CDN被黑客攻陷，下发篡改JS。浏览器对比链上标准哈希不匹配，直接阻断签名。黑客就算拿下全部中心化服务器，也没法欺骗浏览器。

现存现实技术边界（客观局限）

1. 需要适配的浏览器支持DeWEB校验协议。普通浏览器没有内置这套逻辑，需要扩展或者定制浏览器内核。

2. 项目方依然要保管好自己更新前端的私钥，如果项目方私钥泄露，攻击者可以合法链上提交恶意新版本，这属于私钥安全问题，这套机制解决不了私钥泄露。

3. 逻辑层合约漏洞，DeWEB前端上链只管前端不被篡改，不能修复智能合约本身BUG。合约该审计还是要审计。

一句话总结核心价值

过去：合约是可信的，前端是不可信的。黑客专门攻击短板前端。
DeWEB前端上链：把前端完整性校验交给链上晶体管电路做权威基准。浏览器自动校验，补齐整个安全链条最薄弱的前端劫持缺口。

text: People are going to realize it takes a frontier human to extract productivity out of a frontier model, and there is simply not enough frontier human to compensate for the capex relying on revenue from training frontier models (yes if you remove training compute demand the whole thing is unprofitable already, and that’s before token price depreciation). Put it simply, demand for intelligence isn’t infinite and is in the shape of a bell curve, and cheaper models are slowly eating their way into the bell curve, leaving frontier training cost rely on a smaller and smaller tail of intelligence demand. In the end you are left with a billion dollar training run which only use is to solve Navier Stokes, because all the other tasks that are useful for the current economy can be run on cheaper models

text:
inefficiency = free money.

here’s how you can combine Jev and Claude to rank every upcoming catalyst on your watchlist:

1: Get a Jev API key
2: Save the key in a .env file in your project
3: Install TypeSafe's official skill in Claude Code so it knows how to call Jev correctly.
4: Ask Claude Code to set up a project (Python with a TypeSafe key, or TypeScript with a Vercel Gateway key) with separate files for your token watchlist, your Jev questions and your score thresholds.
5: Add a CLAUDE. md file saying that Jev only scores text, code handles all numbers and dates.
6: Have Claude Code build fetchers that collect governance proposals, project announcements, releases and unlock schedules for every token on your watchlist.
7: Convert every item into the same simple record: project, title, text, source link and event date.
8: Calculate how many days away each event is in code, because Jev cannot reliably compare dates.
9: Send each item to Jev in a single call that asks all your questions at once, which keeps it fast and cheap.
10: Ask Jev what type of catalyst it is, how much it could matter, how specific the timing is, and whether it is a recap or just hype.
11: Combine Jev's answers in code into one priority score, using weights you set and can change.
12: Route every item: drop non-catalysts, put unclear ones on a review list, and flag high-priority items and serious security incidents for a brief.
13: Have Claude read the full source for each flagged item and write a short brief.
14: Run it next to your normal research for a week and compare its picks with yours before you trust it.
15: Fix the questions or weights wherever it got things wrong, then test again.
16: Save the workflow as a Claude Skill and set up a scheduled task to run it once or twice a day.

start turning your knowledge into alpha asap.

I can turn this into a detailed guide and an article if this post gets over 100 likes as it will show some interest in creating a catalyst hunting machine.

author: therealchaseeb
quoted_text:
UPDATE:

My portfolio terminal (video is all demo data). One HTML file. No server, no account, no database.

Your entire financial life is AES-256 encrypted in your own browser with a key derived from your password over 1,000,000 PBKDF2 rounds. There's no database for anyone to breach. There's no database at all.

Net worth, cash flow, a full crypto tax ledger with LIFO matching and Form 8949 output. Live prices. 360KB. Zero dependencies.

The seven pages

1 · OVERVIEW — Net worth at a glance, plus a projected total including unvested equity shown before and after tax, so you're never looking at a number you can't actually keep. Treemap allocation, 24h movers split into best and
worst, annual income flow.

2 · HOLDINGS — Every position, any asset class: crypto, equities, cash, property, private funds, receivables. Crypto and equities price themselves off live feeds; everything else you set by hand. Click any cell to edit. One tag
per position turns green when it funds an income stream.

3 · CASH FLOW — Income streams that either sit at a fixed number or yield off a linked position, so a 4.2% T-bill ladder recalculates itself as the balance moves. Burn, waterfall, and a risk-free benchmark pulled from the live
Treasury par yield curve — it tells you when your "yield" is losing to a 3-month bill.

4 · TRADING — The crypto ledger. Every acquisition with its cost basis, every disposal, and where you stand: realized gains split short vs long term for the year, unrealized on open lots as of right now. Two clocks, labelled,
never blurred.

5 · HISTORY — A year of portfolio value as a trace, plus an audit log of every single change ever made — every buy, revalue, reclass, rename, parameter change — timestamped.

6 · TAX — Reads the trading ledger and produces an actual return. LIFO matching, Form 8949 Part I/II with box mapping, §1211(b) $3,000 offset, character-preserving loss carryforward. Quarterly estimated payments, and a
reconciliation waterfall from income → taxed → owed → paid, where every line links back to where the figure came from.

7 · SYSTEM — One tax rate that governs every page. Growth and withdrawal assumptions, API keys, and encrypted .enc export/import so your backup is as unreadable as your vault.

这个阶段，
不回购、不销毁、不推迟团队解锁的项目，
我基本都不会太关注。

因为现在这个市场，光讲故事已经不太够了。
所以今天看到 0G 的公告，
我第一眼其实没去看 ComFi，
反而先看了另一条：
团队 + 早期投资人的 44% 代币，首次解锁延期一年。
——————————————————————
总量不变 → 按月线性释放 → 24 个月 → 整体往后推一年
这意味着，
原本下个月就要面对的 44% 新增供给，现在暂时不用面对了。
短期新增流通筹码和潜在抛压，自然也少了很多。
——————————————————————
另一边，0G 又推出了 Compute Finance（ComFi），
尝试把数字资产和 AI 算力使用权连接起来。
目前 Ascend 已上线：
0G → 质押 → a0G → 铸造 iAI → 质押 iAI → Compute Credits → 使用 AI
其中：
·a0G = 目前唯一可以铸造 iAI 的资产
·iAI = 计划 9 月 29 日上线
Compute Credits 后续可以用于：
·0G Private Computer / 0G App
·Private Computer 目前提供 100+ 模型。
所以我现在看 0G，主要就是两条线：
供给端：44% 团队 + 早期投资人筹码延期。
需求端：ComFi 能不能真正带来 AI 使用需求。

毕竟 Crypto 最不缺的就是叙事。
我更关心后面能不能看到：
真实用户 → Compute 消耗 → 协议收入 → zero-gravity:native 价值捕获
叙事决定有没有人看，资金决定有没有行情，产业地位决定能走多远，最后还是要回到真实需求。
——————————————————————
而到了新周期，
我觉得真正值得放进观察列表的标的，
反而会越来越少。
RWA、DeFi、Perps、AI（隐私），
可能会成为接下来需要重点关注的几条主线。
但主线下面，最终还是要回到：
谁有叙事、谁有资金、谁有位置，谁又真的能把需求（拉盘）跑出来。

author: xicilion
quoted_text:
很多人每天都在写 JavaScript，但 JS 最初只能运行在浏览器里给网页做点动效。直到 2009 年，Ryan Dahl 把谷歌 Chrome 里的 V8 引擎抽出来，外层用 C++ 包装了一套系统调用和事件循环，做出了 Node.js。从那一天起，JavaScript 才能在服务器上读写文件、监听网络端口，正式变成了全栈语言。

Node.js 统治了服务端开发十几年，但随着前端工程越来越复杂，整个工具链变得沉重。写 TypeScript 得装编译器，打包要配构建工具，跑测试要装测试框架，依赖动辄塞满几个 G 的 node_modules 目录。工具链被割裂成七零八落的碎片，项目启动和打包越来越慢。

后来开发者 Jarred Sumner 决定重新写一个运行时，这就是 Bun。Bun 做了一件很大胆的事：它没有沿用 V8，选用了苹果 WebKit 的底层引擎 JavaScriptCore，这个引擎启动速度极快。同时 Bun 把包管理器、打包工具、测试运行器和 TypeScript 解释器全部打包进一个单文件二进制里，开箱即用。为了把性能压榨到极致，Bun 底层选择了新兴系统级语言 Zig，直接跑出比 Node.js 快数倍的成绩。

但随着项目代码膨胀到几十万行，一个隐蔽的系统级矛盾浮出了水面：内存管理方式冲突。JavaScript 这一层依赖自动垃圾回收（GC），开发者从来不需要手动释放对象；而底层用来写胶水层和网络调用的 Zig，是类似 C 语言的手动内存管理，申请和释放内存全凭工程师的人肉心智。当上层的自动垃圾回收和底层的指针手动释放纠缠在一起，指针悬挂（use-after-free）和重复释放（double-free）层出不穷，经常导致底层进程莫名其妙崩溃。

修这类内存 Bug 耗费了大量精力，于是团队做出了一个重要决定：把整个底层从 Zig 换成 Rust。Rust 在运行时性能上能与 Zig 保持平齐，更重要的是它有一套所有权机制与借用检查器。如果一段代码存在内存被提前释放后又被访问的风险，Rust 在编译阶段就直接报错拒绝构建，把原本需要在线上抓耳挠腮排查的崩溃问题，直接消灭在本地编译期。

把 53.5 万行复杂的底层系统代码换一种语言重写，按以往经验往往需要几十人团队折腾一两年。加入 Anthropic 后的 Bun 团队换了一种搞法，借助 Claude Code 拉起 64 个并发实例，在不同的 git worktree 里分工执行自动化转换、类型对齐和对抗性测试。花了 11 天时间重构完 1448 个文件，消耗约 16.5 万美元的 Token，跑通了 99.8% 的测试用例。

从 Node.js 用 C++ 封装 V8 打开服务端大门，到 Bun 用 Zig 追求极致执行速度，再到如今引入 Rust 的编译器解决内存安全，底层运行时的演进一直在探索速度、开发体验与系统稳定性之间的平衡点。

text:
美联储的加息逻辑是否还适用于当前这个“AI军备竞赛”时代？这是比尔.阿克曼这篇推文的核心思考。阿克曼想表达什么？
1、传统央行逻辑是：
加息 → 借款成本上升 → 消费和投资下降 → 总需求降温 → 通胀回落。

2、阿克曼提出一个“如果”：
1）现在对算力和能源的需求，几乎不受利率高低影响。因为谁赢得超级智能（AGI）竞赛，回报接近无限大，ROI高到可以忽略资金成本，所以加息压不下来这块投资；
2）但加息会把利息成本嵌进所有商品和服务的价格里（企业融资更贵、政府债务利息更高，最终转嫁给消费者）；
3）结果可能是：加息不但没压通胀，反而推高通胀 → 美联储不得不继续加 → 形成恶性循环；

他的结论：旧模型可能已经不适用，美联储这次加息可能是错的。当然他也只是一个思考和设问。

3、个人角度这个逻辑部分有道理
有道理的地方：
1）AI资本开支确实有一定利率不敏感。微软、谷歌、亚马逊、Meta等超大规模公司为了抢AGI，正在砸巨资建数据中心、买芯片、扩能源，预期回报极高时，资金成本上升不会立刻让他们停手。能源需求也被AI拉动；

2）利率本身是生产成本的一部分（这叫做货币政策的“成本渠道”cost channel）。企业借钱囤库存、建数据中心，利率升高会推高边际成本，部分会转嫁到价格上；

3）如果通胀主要来自供给侧短缺（住房、算力、医疗、能源），加息抑制供给的一面，确实可能恶化短缺；

当前通胀脉冲很大一部分是能源/地缘政治（中东冲突推高油价），不完全是美联储能单独解决的，也不是单纯需求过热。

但也有站不住的地方：
1）AI投资也是经济的一部分。 住房、汽车、耐用品、中小企业投资、消费者信贷，这些对利率非常敏感。加息会冷却这些领域的需求；

2）2022–2023年美联储把利率从接近0加到5%以上，CPI从9%降到3%左右。土耳其当时反向操作（土耳其央行认为高利率导致通胀，随意大幅度降息），通胀飙到80%。

当然21-22年大通胀首要事来自疫情的供给（海运成本飙升）+无限量量化宽松带来的需求飙升+还有22年上半年俄乌战争导致油价走高又加了一棒；

4、应该怎么理解
可以把阿克曼说的当成一个有启发性的问题
当前宏观环境的特殊性在于：AI正在同时制造短期需求冲击（建数据中心、抢电力、抢芯片）和潜在长期供给改善（生产率提升）。沃什之前也强调AI长期是通缩力量，但短期需求先到、生产率后到，所以通胀粘性更强。

这核心是一个时间差的逻辑，AI基建浪潮是钱先花出去，推高整个AI基建产业链上所有环节的价格（当下正在发生的）+叠加今年的能源问题（也是之前说的今年通胀的核心问题是油价），确实会让美联储短期内很难精准调控。加息不能让AI基建冷却下来、但是可以让非AI需求冷却，那么对冲下来则会让通胀不那么强。

未来如果AI最终带来巨大生产率提升，通胀压力也会自己缓解。所以争辩联储当下的加息可能意义也不大（毕竟已经发生了），核心是去看两点：
短期的能源冲击合适会缓解？
长期AI带动全社会生产率的提升何时到来？

之前8月底聊过AI存在四个时钟（时间差）、宏观生产率的提升恰恰就是最后一个兑现的时钟。 https://t.co/GqUQgBZxs3
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
The presumption that the Fed raising short-term rates reduces inflation is predicated on the belief that higher rates reduce demand and investment. 

But what if higher rates don’t reduce demand and investment because the demand for intelligence and energy is unaffected by higher rates because winning the race for super intelligence has a near infinite ROI and the demand for compute will remain incalculable. 

Why won’t higher rates at this unique moment in history therefore lead to more inflation as interest costs are embedded in everything? 

And the problem is compounded as the more the Fed raises rates, the more inflation we will have and the more the Fed will need to raise rates further and so on. 

But what if the old models don’t apply to the current paradigm and the Fed is wrong?

I think the Fed might have just made a mistake. Am I right or am I wrong?

Ethena is partnering with @Binance as our first venue for the extension of the basis trade into equity perpetuals, one of the most exciting updates to the USDe collateral backing since launch.

Binance equity basis has averaged ~11%+ annualized over the past 6 months, while open interest has grown on average ~30% per month in the last 3 month period.

We expect the market opportunity size for equity perpetuals to far exceed the $15b+ of crypto perpetuals captured by Ethena last cycle.

Allocations begin today.

Var 我前期玩了一下就停了，基本没分。

但这个机会我还不想放。现在能上车的就两条路：场外买分，或者去预测市场赌 FDV。

场外最近大概 20–30U / 分。  
8–9 月大单多在 20–26U，9 月 10 号、13 号两笔十万 U 级别成交卡在 20U。代币经济 9 月 23 号一出，盘口抬到 24–32U，这几天有人按 25U 卖，也有人按 30U 在算。

另一条是 Polymarket。TGE 只写了 Q4，没给日子。

按每周固定发 15 万分算：  
Q3 结束大约 915 万  
最早 Q4（10 月初）：915–930 万  
最晚 Q4（12 月底）：大约 1110 万

用现在场外 25–30U 反推，空投池大约 2.3–3.3 亿 U。  
32% 全解锁的话，对应 FDV 大概只有 7–10 亿。  
盘口给的中位数是 15 亿，超过 20 亿大概三分之一概率。

所以我这边没去追 25–30U 的分，直接买了大量 FDV 低于 20 亿。

这个第一天抛压应该不会小，后面不好说。

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
$e/acc rise itself is not the biggest benefit for $PAID. It is more like a very successful Product Demo, showing that UsePaid’s Fee Flow is beginning to be validated by multiple projects.

98kfF7rmsg1QDUEoCqNE7g7M1FdrTt92TEp2CLzypump 

My analysis is as follows:One of the most direct catalysts for PAID this time is e/acc:

e/acc Trading → Creator Fees → UsePaid → 80% X Money → Beff
20% → Buy PAID → Burn

The e/acc case proves that a Token’s trading fees can be converted into real-world X Money Funding through UsePaid, while part of the funds flows back into PAID.

But more importantly, we can no longer look at e/acc alone.

Paid officially published its Top Paid Launches:

parafactual: $2.33M MC → $30,513 sent to parafactual
CALI: $2.22M MC → $49,965 sent to mayemusk
ELON: $681K MC → $10,759 sent to elonmusk
SOLCAT: $164K MC → $70,690 sent to solana
BOAR: $91K MC → $39,588 sent to nikitabier

The five projects have generated approximately $201K in actual payments in total.

The most important point is not the market caps of these Tokens, but that Paid Launches have started to evolve from a single case into multiple real cases.

So I believe the fundamental narrative has already started to change:

The market may currently only see:

e/acc → Beff → X Money

But eventually it could become:

Multiple Tokens → Creator Fees → UsePaid → X Money → Internet Figures

This means UsePaid is beginning to validate its core product logic:

Token Trading → Creator Fees → Real-world Funding → Attention

And PAID sits on the other side of the funding flow:

Creator Fees → 20% Buy PAID → Burn

So PAID’s real value-capture logic is:

UsePaid Launches ↑ → Trading Volume ↑ → Creator Fees ↑ → PAID Buyback ↑ → PAID Burn ↑ → Supply ↓

This is why I say e/acc’s rise itself is not the biggest benefit for PAID, but is more like a very successful Product Demo.

Because if e/acc were the only case, the market would still be trading:

Beff Attention → e/acc → PAID

But after the emergence of multiple Paid Launches such as parafactual, CALI, ELON, SOLCAT, and BOAR, the logic starts becoming:

One Successful Case → Multiple Successful Cases → Product Validation → Platform Narrative

This could change how the market values PAID.

Previously, the market may have been trading:

PAID = A Meme Token

Now it is starting to trade:

PAID = UsePaid Platform / Fee-Buyback Asset

In addition, the catalysts behind PAID’s rise this time can be broken down into three layers.

The first layer is the e/acc breakout.

e/acc became a high-exposure case for Beff, generated significant Creator Fees, and sent a large amount of funding to Beff through X Money, allowing the market to directly see:

Token → Creator → X Money → Real Funding

And PAID, as the buyback side of this funding flow, naturally gained attention.

The second layer is Paid officially publishing the Top Paid Launches.

This proves that UsePaid is not just about e/acc. Multiple projects have already generated actual payments, ranging from around $10K to nearly $70K, showing that Paid Launches are beginning to form a multi-project Fee Flow network.

The third layer is the market beginning to reprice PAID’s value capture.

If more Paid Launches appear in the future:

More Tokens → More Volume → More Creator Fees → More X Money Payments → More PAID Buyback/Burn

then PAID’s value will no longer depend entirely on a single Meme, but will begin to depend on the trading volume of the entire UsePaid ecosystem.

So what the market is really betting on now is:

PAID → UsePaid → Creator Funding Infrastructure → X Money → Internet Figures

In other words, the market is betting on whether UsePaid can become a new Creator Funding / Attention Settlement Layer.

The traditional Meme logic is:Token → Attention → Price

UsePaid’s logic is:Token → Trading → Fees → Creator Funding → Attention → More Trading

And with PAID added:Fees → PAID Buyback → Burn

The complete loop becomes:

Token Launches ↑ → Trading Volume ↑ → Creator Fees ↑ → X Money Funding ↑ → More Creators / Figures Participate ↑ → Attention ↑ → More Token Launches ↑ → PAID Buyback ↑ → Burn ↑

What is really worth watching next is not simply PAID’s market cap, but the number of Paid Launches, total Creator Fees / X Money payments, and PAID Buyback / Burn.

The current $201K in actual payments is an important validation point. If this grows from $200K to $1M and then $10M, while PAID Buybacks and Burns grow alongside it, then PAID’s fundamentals will strengthen further.

Of course, the biggest risk remains:UsePaid Product Success ≠ PAID Token Value

Even if UsePaid generates a large amount of Creator Fees, we still need to confirm how much of that actually goes into PAID Buyback/Burn. Creators receiving money also does not mean PAID holders own those funds, revenue, or equity.

So what ultimately needs to be validated is:UsePaid Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → PAID Buyback ↑ → Burn ↑

rather than simply:UsePaid Attention ↑ → PAID Price ↑

So the biggest change in my view of PAID’s positioning is:Before: PAID = UsePaid’s Meme Token

Now: PAID = Value-Capture Token for UsePaid Creator Funding Infrastructure

And the Top Paid Launches data this time is an important piece of evidence supporting this shift.

Chart: https://t.co/ooNHXxVVXG

text:
不要用你的民科认知去挑战科学。一些生酮饮食与胰腺炎关联的核心文献，按研究类型分类整理：

### 病例报告

**1. Buse GJ, et al. *Current Surgery*. 2004.**
*   **标题**：Patient with gemfibrozil-controlled hypertriglyceridemia that developed acute pancreatitis after starting ketogenic diet.
*   **核心发现**：一名甘油三酯经吉非贝齐控制良好的患者，在开始高脂生酮饮食后数天发生急性胰腺炎。结论明确指出生酮饮食可能导致血清甘油三酯大幅升高，从而在脂质代谢异常者中诱发胰腺炎。

**2. Chan JT, et al. *Cureus*. 2022.**
*   **标题**：Severe Hypertriglyceridemia-Induced Necrotizing Pancreatitis Associated With Ketogenic Diet in a Well-Controlled Patient With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
*   **核心发现**：一名19岁血糖控制良好的2型糖尿病男性，在无监督生酮饮食3个月后，发生严重高甘油三酯血症诱发的坏死性胰腺炎，此前无高甘油三酯病史。

**3. 伊朗病例报告（Clinical Nutrition Open Science, 2023）**
*   **标题**：Inducing necrotizing pancreatitis associated with a ketogenic diet: A case report.
*   **核心发现**：一名48岁肥胖男性（有家族性高脂血症史）在严格生酮饮食45天后，甘油三酯飙升至 **7891 mg/dL**，确诊为高甘油三酯血症诱发的急性坏死性胰腺炎。

**4. Mori M, et al. *Brain & Development*. 2021.**
*   **标题**：Ketogenic diet for refractory epilepsy with MEHMO syndrome: Caution for acute necrotizing pancreatitis.
*   **核心发现**：一名5岁MEHMO综合征患儿，在生酮饮食联合胰岛素治疗期间发生致命性急性坏死性胰腺炎，最终死亡。提示特定基因缺陷人群对生酮饮食的胰腺毒性更为敏感。

### 临床观察性研究

**5. Ahmed Ward HS, et al. *QJM: An International Journal of Medicine*. 2024.**
*   **标题**：Pancreatic Affection in Children on Ketogenic Diet.
*   **核心发现**：一项前瞻性观察研究，对20名接受生酮饮食的耐药性癫痫患儿随访。结果显示**血清淀粉酶和脂肪酶在生酮饮食3个月后显著升高（p < 0.001）**，6个月后回落。虽未出现临床胰腺炎病例，但证实生酮饮食对胰腺存在亚临床生化影响。

**6. Jung DE, et al. *Brain & Development*. 2012.**
*   **标题**：Safety and role of ketogenic parenteral nutrition for intractable childhood epilepsy.
*   **核心发现**：10名接受生酮肠外营养的患儿中，**1例出现淀粉酶和脂肪酶升高**，并因此停用；另1例甘油三酯升高至 **1885 mg/dL**。

### 动物实验与机制研究

**7. Xia H, et al. *Nutrients*. 2023.**
*   **标题**：Ketogenic Diet Exacerbates L-Arginine-Induced Acute Pancreatitis and Reveals the Therapeutic Potential of Butyrate.
*   **核心发现**：小鼠实验表明，生酮饮食通过**破坏肠道屏障、改变肠道菌群（Lachnospirales和Erysipelotrichales富集）、耗竭短链脂肪酸**，加重了急性胰腺炎的严重程度。补充丁酸盐可逆转这一效应。

### 综述与临床指南

**8. Dyńka D, et al. *Annals of Medicine*. 2026.**
*   **标题**：The ketogenic diet is not for everyone: contraindications, side effects, and drug interactions.
*   **核心结论**：将**急性胰腺炎列为生酮饮食的相对禁忌症**。指出高脂生酮饮食可能加重脂肪吸收不良并恶化症状，在胰腺炎急性期后若考虑使用生酮饮食，需临床研究验证其安全性。

**9. *CMAJ* (Canadian Medical Association Journal). 2024.**
*   **标题**：Acute pancreatitis caused by severe hypertriglyceridemia in a 61-year-old man on a carnivore diet.
*   **核心发现**：在病因分类表中明确将**生酮或肉食饮食（饱和脂肪过量）列为高甘油三酯血症的饮食因素**，并指出该患者可能因多因素乳糜微粒血症（受胰岛素抵抗、甲减及肉食饮食共同加剧）而诱发急性胰腺炎。

author: bubbleboi
quoted_text:
First off remember that there are two options if it's going out from IB - the payment for order flow (which IB may match internally or route to dealer/MM) or exchange. So as MM to get IB order you're already adverse selected on one hurdle (IB didn't match internal), rest of street could've seen it (and may have passed on it), and I'm now holding it. And, IB lot that id see as a dealer is probably someone like you - not HFT ping pong. 

I need to look at 505/506 data - I can send you a chart pack when I dig it up - but my modeling of markups/PFoF used IB as the proxy/control versus dumb money retail, it's basically the opposite of robinhood flow all things considered, and partially because of their model. 

As a MM, I'm going to have some buckets of predictable flow:
- Money manager type accounts who are one-way in a name; VWAP/TWAP orders, perhaps, or I'm talking to them and I know 
- Option-driven, index-driven (which is the offset, here AP create-redeem more important)
- Much of what is thematic / the herd is one directional 
- Pods, which all herd and I'm basically playing a momentum game against them and waiting for their blow ups to monetize, but which I can predict - if pod A is buyer at 11am, pod B will be at 11:15 (esp if they have any momentum-type pricing - usually it's clusters of them coming in off each other, it is very amusing in practice)

An IB order is the most likely to be informed, yes - because it has broad retail access AND funds can route through it.

If I'm at a large dealer, they're a broker. They're not a client. They have a sales rep, probably, but I'm going to treat them as an adversary, the brokers still pick you off. The client did not route to me - I do not get (necessarily) a promise of a future trade or relationship benefits - nor do I have a sales guy who has an idea of why you're executing. 

Bursty random flow - even if "unintelligent" - can still be quite toxic, as well. 

If one of my clients is doing a large trade - and large in market impact - and he says he's done, then he goes sells more on another venue, that's toxic/unpredictable, hurts my ability to hedge/distribute. 

And a routing from a broker is max adverse selection because IB will just route across street as treated the same. So also scenario where if I'm not axed and getting hit by a broker, I'm going to widen out, usually you look into that & assume something went wrong, you were quoting poorly, there was some arb (again, broadly but maybe less the case in cash equities - brokers are actually the worse for dealers - because, here I'm talking less liquid markets/derivs/swaps experience, many of them pick you off when your quoting is off/look for arbs, because there's no trust relationship). 

So if you were sending in your order, I may see this 50k lot from IB, but if it was my client, I may be able to have them TWAP/VWAP it and that is what makes it predictable. Basically intraday 15 minute reset TWAP/VWAP - distance from here is "is MM pissed off", to simplify. 

I worked for one of the large dealers and sat by the algo sales traders on the equity side + covered some large etrading accounts on the treasury side.

Bitgetは、9月24日に確認されたセキュリティインシデントを受け、出金を段階的に再開します。

text:
Everyone wants to know which of the Magnificent Seven AI kills. I think that’s the wrong question.

None of them need to disappear.

IBM didn’t disappear. Intel didn’t disappear. They just stopped being the scarce asset in the next computing cycle.

AI has three layers that matter:

Who owns the intelligence: models and data.

Who owns the factory: chips, power and cloud.

Who owns the last mile: the device, workplace, feed or agent where demand starts.

The obvious conclusion is that Apple and Microsoft have more to defend than most people think. Apple owns the device but rents much of the intelligence. Microsoft owns enormous enterprise distribution, but agents are coming directly for the software seat.

But there’s another side to this that I think matters even more.

The AI infrastructure trade isn’t seven different bets if they all depend on the same customer paying the bill.

NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC, the clouds and the AI labs can look diversified on a screen while ultimately depending on the same AI capex cycle.

Picks and shovels are only safe when the miners can pay.

That was one of the lessons of 2000. Equipment demand looked enormous until the financing underneath the customers broke.

I don’t think AI is 2000. The demand is real and the technology is real. But the financing still matters.

So I’ve stopped asking only which company wins AI.

I’m asking which companies still compound if the AI capex cycle slows for two years.

That gives me a very different list.

author: sjdedic
quoted_text:
read the SEC's new crypto assets FAQ

the securities laws are starting to look opt-in now, at least as applied by the SEC to crypto

if you raise money by selling a non-rights-bearing token, are careful about what you represent or promise, and have a functional crypto system, there is now an extremely broad path outside the securities laws--arguably 'functionality' is not even necessary but there's some equivocation on this

the buyback guidance goes further than I expected. once the system is functional, even announcing a token buyback *program* (which I guess even could be a 'perpetual program') does not, in the staff's view, constitute a promise of essential managerial efforts. same for promises to improve the system or grow its network effects

so you can retain enormous influence over the thing, keep developing it, support its price with buybacks (including under a permanent "program"), and get many of the benefits of having a public investment instrument, without giving holders the rights or protections that normally come with one

they have opened a loophole in a regulatory regime whose whole point was supposed to be that you couldn't draft your way around economic reality (see e.g. https://t.co/mrH9hPUUMU)

can't really say if this is good or bad, but VCs etc. got a lot of what they wanted & the market should absorb all the implications of this

among others, I am growing skeptical how much of a 'long tail' there will be for tokenized equity. . .if you can get people to buy a coin in the style of BNB, HYPE, PUMP, etc., with minimal regulation, why voluntarily take on the burdens of selling them equity? if you are not mag-7 level, it doesn't seem there would be much reason to focus on equity securities for your capital-raising. . . if you want to access 'traditional buyers' you can wrap the token in an equity instrument like an ADR for those institutions. . . 

the obvious next question is how far this extends beyond crypto businesses. can an ordinary company attach a functional token to its business and apply 100% of its profits to discretionary buybacks, without giving holders any right to those profits or making representations about future business efforts that independently trigger Howey? the FAQ doesn't expressly resolve that, but it opens a pretty enormous door

equity still gives investors something a discretionary buyback token doesn't. . .the question is whether the market will pay enough for those rights to make granting them worthwhile. otherwise the incentive is to keep the equity for insiders and sell everyone else the coin

crypto's current focus on hyping tokenized equity may be misguided, the bigger trend is "get all the benefits of equity with none of the burdens"

of course this is SEC guidance, not a repeal of the statutes or a command to the courts. a private plaintiff or a future SEC could have other ideas

but did not think I'd see it in my lifetime. . .the securities laws are being "disrupted" in substantial part by incentivizing making fewer commitments to investors. and if Warren Dems eventually take control and try to undo all this, after an entire market has organized around it, the resulting chaos will be something to behold

text:
美国30年固定房贷利率又回到了7%以上

美国人现在贷款买房利息又变贵了。30年固定房贷利率从前一周的6.97%，涨到7.12%，是2024年5月以来最高的水平。

举个例子，同样借40万美元，分30年还，利率6%的时候，每个月大约还2,398美元，到了7.12%，每个月就要还2,694美元，一年多还约3,500美元。这还只是还给银行的本金和利息，没有算房产税和保险。

如果工资没涨，每个月还银行的钱却多了，其他地方就得少花一点。有些人会少出去吃饭、少旅游，有些人会推迟换车、换家电，还有些人干脆先不买房。这样的人越来越多，商家能做的生意也就可能变少，收入也会变低。

买房少了，影响的也不只是卖房的人。搬家公司、装修工人、卖家具家电的，都可能少一些生意。如果新房一直不好卖，开发商也可能少盖一些房子，建筑工人和卖建材的也会受到影响。公司可能不会立刻裁员，但可能先不招新人，或者减少加班，员工能赚到的钱就可能变少。

所以前面的PMI说企业现在生意还不错，和这里说买房越来越贵，可以同时发生。只要工作稳定、工资还在涨，一部分家庭还能承担。但如果后面工作难找了、工资不怎么涨了，房贷又一直这么贵，买房和花钱的人就可能进一步减少，企业的生意也会跟着更难做。

经济也就会越来越差。

刚刚下跌是因为 十年期 美债收益率暴力拉升，已经到了 5.087% ，背后的触发因素包括刚公布的美国 PMI，9月综合指数从上个月的 56 升至 58.4，企业投入成本指数也从 59.9 升至 66.4。说人话就是企业的订单和生意都在增加，但成本上涨也在加快，经济表现越强，美联储越有底气继续加息，而成本继续上涨，又让市场担心通胀没有那么容易降下来。

对于美股来说，美债能提供更高的到期收益率，投资者就会要求股票提供更高的回报，同样的盈利预期，也就更难让资金接受原来的股价。同时，企业发行新债、旧债到期续借的成本也可能跟着提高，尤其是那些还在大量借钱扩张的公司，未来需要拿出更多收入支付利息。

Bitcoin 和其他加密货币也会受到这种环境影响，资金对回报的要求提高、承担波动的意愿下降，愿意继续追高的买盘就可能减少。

所以即便下一次议息会议还没到，市场也可以先把长期借钱的成本抬上去，不能认为上一次加息落地后，利率带来的影响就结束了。接下来要看十年期收益率能否回落，还是会持续停留在 5% 以上并继续上行。

如果再叠加油价上涨，市场就需要同时消化能源成本增加和利率维持高位的影响，美股和加密市场的反弹也会面临更多阻力。

text:
Looking closely at LONG post, the core is not simply a normal product update. It is that LONG is starting to build a shared asset pool across the Stock-Paired ecosystem for $AI.

LONG currently supports 70+ Tokenized Stocks. In the new Stock-Paired Launch, 5% of Stock Token Fees goes into the AI Community Vault, while another 5% is used to buy back and burn the Token paired with the stock, while LP continues to compound automatically.

So the original logic:Stock Pair → Trading → Liquidity → LONG Ecosystem Growth

Now becomes:Stock Pair → Trading → Fees → AI Reserve

In other words, when a new Stock-Paired project grows, it not only gains liquidity and trading volume itself, but the AI Community Vault also continuously accumulates Tokenized Stock assets as the ecosystem expands.

This is what LONG means by “S&P 500 of tokenized stocks.” It does not mean AI becomes an actual ETF or stock index. Rather, the goal is to use a large number of Stock-Paired Markets to aggregate the economic activity generated by different stock assets into a shared AI Community Reserve. LONG currently supports 70+ Tokenized Stocks.

More importantly, this changes the original competitive relationship within the LONG ecosystem.

Previously:AI vs MONITOR vs BONER vs other Stock-Paired Tokens

Everyone was competing for liquidity, trading volume, and attention.

Now:New Stock Pair → Trading Growth → 5% Stock Fees → AI Reserve Growth

So the more successful a new project becomes, the more assets the AI Community Vault can accumulate.

This is what LONG refers to as PvE:New Project Growth → AI Reserve Growth → AI Community has more incentive to support new projects → More Projects Enter LONG → Reserve Continues Growing

The official mechanism is designed to give AI holders a reason to discover and support new Stock Communities, while new projects gain access to an existing community whose Reserve also benefits from their activity.

So the positioning of AI is also starting to change.

Previously:AI / NVDA Stock-Paired Meme

Now it is starting to evolve toward:LONG Ecosystem RWA Community Reserve

And Nate’s post:“gLONG locked in. flow state. you know what's coming next. for now I'd share one word long 500”

does not introduce a new mechanism by itself, but when viewed alongside the official LONG 500 announcement, it clearly appears to be previewing a larger product phase.

So when the two posts are combined, the key flywheel is:More Stock Pairs → More Trading → More Fees → AI Reserve ↑ → AI Community Strength ↑ → More Support for New Stock Communities → More Stock Pairs

At the same time, each new Pair has its own loops:Trading → 5% Buyback/Burn → Supply ↓

and:Trading → LP Compounding → Liquidity ↑ → More Trading

So there are now effectively three layers:

Layer 1: Individual Token

Trading → Buyback/Burn → Liquidity

Layer 2: LONG

More Stock Pairs → More Trading → More Liquidity → More Fees

Layer 3: AI

More Stock Communities → More Stock Fees → $AI Reserve ↑

This is the real upgrade behind LONG 500.

Previously, LONG was mainly building Stock-Paired Liquidity Infrastructure.

Now it is adding:Liquidity Infrastructure → Asset Accumulation → Community Reserve

One important point, however: growth of the AI Reserve does not mean AI holders directly own these stocks or have legal rights to their proceeds. The first thing that needs to be validated is whether this Reserve can actually continue accumulating assets as the LONG ecosystem grows.

The three most important metrics to watch next are:

1. Whether the number and value of Tokenized Stocks in the AI Community Vault continue to grow

2. Whether LONG’s new Stock-Paired Markets and trading volume continue to grow

3. Whether the 5% Stock Fee is consistently converted into AI Reserve accumulation

If these three things actually take off, LONG 500 will no longer just be a Narrative. It will become a new economic flywheel within the LONG ecosystem.

In one sentence:LONG 500 is beginning to turn part of the asset flow generated by its Liquidity Network into a AI Community Reserve.

text:
Everyone on planet Earth is talking about local AI right now

And for good reason

Governments are banning models. Hardware prices are 10xing

You NEED to be getting into local AI. The number 1 questions everyone has though is which computer to buy?

Here's your answer:

You basically have 3 options:

1. MAC STUDIO (high intelligence, lower speeds)-

Mac Studios are excellent devices for local AI. They can run MASSIVE models. I'm running GLM 5.2 right now on a single Mac Studio. The model is Opus 4.8 level

The issue is, Mac Studios are a bit slower at running intelligence (altho the M5 Ultra is promising)

Mac Studios are a good choice for you if you want frontier level intelligence, but are fine running the intelligence passively

Meaning you get top intelligence, but it runs more in the background rather than on demand

As an example, I have GLM 5.2 running security checks on my codebase every hour. It creates a report. I review this later in the day

2. POWERHOUSE NVIDIA CHIPS (RTX 5090, 6000 Pro)

Nvidia is the most valuable company in the world, and for good reason

They make the world's best GPUs.

They have decent VRAM (32gb on the 5090, 96gb on the 6000 Pro) and INSANE bandwidth. Meaning the local models run at unbelievable speeds

I'm running Qwen 3.8 locally on a 5090 and it's just as fast as cloud models

I'd go this route if you want to run an AI agent like Hermes off a local model, still get decent intelligence, but have it able to work lightning fast

3. AI WORKSTATIONS (DGX Spark type computers)

The DGX Spark is an excellent AI computer

It has high memory (128gb unified memory) and has decent speeds because of the Nvidia CUDA architecture

It is basically the sweet spot between a cutting edge Nvidia chip and a Mac Studio

You can run medium sized models, and get usable speeds out of them

You're not going to get the same performance as cloud models, but it will allow you to offload small secondary tasks to your local models for them to handle

They are also the absolute easiest to get up and running

You plug it in, then tell your agent on your main computer to go onto it and set it up. You don't even need it connected to a monitor

CONCLUSION

Here's what it comes down to: how high intelligence do you need, what speeds do you need, and how plug and play do you want?

Want the highest speeds, like you are used to with cloud compute? Build a computer around an RTX 5090

Want to run frontier level intelligence, and don't mind slower speeds, go with a Mac Studio

Either way, it's never been more important to get into local AI
