author: serverConnectd
quoted_text:
Muse will be the top installed app for a while thanks to Meta’s distribution might..

But they are starting to have a retention issue: most people still don’t know what to do with a personal agent, so they lose interest after a while. 

I bet Muse will get much more proactive rather than reactive like it is today:

“I can take care of this for you. Want me to?”

I think there are a LOT of money saving opportunities in finance

“Your credit card is charging 27% interest. You qualify for a much cheaper way to pay it off. Want me to move it?”

“You have $8,000 sitting in checking earning almost nothing. Want me to move the excess to a higher-yield account?”

“You’re paying off three debts. Putting your extra $300 toward this one first will save the most interest. Want me to change the payments?”

“Your car insurance just went up 22%. Want me to shop for a cheaper policy?”

“You’re paying for two subscriptions you haven’t used in months. Want me to cancel them?”

“Your employer will match another 2% of your 401(k) contributions. Want me to increase it?”

“Your credit card annual fee is coming up, but you barely used the benefits. Want me to downgrade it?”

Other non finance examples:

“Your kid’s soccer practice moved to 6:30. Want me to tell your spouse and update the calendar?”

“This group chat has been trying to pick a restaurant for three days. Friday at 7 works for everyone. Want me to book it?”

“Your package is delayed and will now arrive while you’re at work. Want me to change the delivery?”

“Your sister’s birthday is Saturday. Here are three gift ideas under $50.”

“You usually order groceries on Sunday. Want me to rebuild last week’s cart?”

“You told your friend you’d send them those photos. Want me to do it?”

“You’re running late for dinner. Want me to text the group your ETA?”

“One of the Marketplace couches you saved just dropped $100. Want me to message the seller?”

“Your flight is delayed. Want me to tell the person picking you up?”

“You’ve been trying to make plans with three friends. Saturday afternoon is the only time everyone is free. Want me to organize it?”

“Your dentist asked you to reschedule. I found three open appointments that work with your calendar. Pick one?”

“Your child’s school sent a permission slip due Friday. Want me to remind you tonight?”

“You said you need to return something to Target. The return window closes in four days. Want me to remind you when you’re near one?”

Basically moving from: You think of a task → you ask → AI helps.

To:
AI notices something → suggests an action → you approve.

Then you trust it and Muse handles routine things automatically and tells you afterward.

IMO people aren’t going to keep opening an agent because it can answer questions, unless they are subbing muse for ChatGPT; I don’t think it’s there yet…

They’ll keep opening it because it keeps saving them time, remembering things they forgot, and taking annoying little tasks off their plate.

text:
Claude Code effort 설정 가이드(@trq212)

Terminal-Bench 3.0 HTML 새니타이저 과제 성공률 low 1/5 → xhigh 5/5

---

1. effort는 뭘 바꾸나

모델이 과제에 쓸 연산량의 근사치. effort가 올라갈수록 Claude가 스스로 판단하고 검증·엣지케이스 테스트를 하는 비중이 커진다고 함.

같은 일을 12시간 주면 끝까지 파고들고, 1시간 주면 쓸 만한 버전부터 내고 다듬는다는 비유. 즉, 지능 다이얼보다는 검증량 다이얼에 가깝다고 봄

---

2. 사양이 모호할수록 차이가 커짐

"피트니스 앱 만들어줘"만 던지면 low는 기록+그래프, max는 히트맵까지 붙임. /config 메뉴 리디자인은 low 1분에 스케치, max 28분에 실제 제품 수준 목업.

반면 인터뷰로 상세 사양을 먼저 만들면 effort 간 결과가 거의 비슷해짐. effort를 올리기 전에 사양부터 잘 쓰는 게 먼저인 경우가 많은듯

---

3. 어려운 과제에선 엣지케이스가 승부처

Opus 5.5 기준 low → high/xhigh
스토리지 엔진 버그 수정 0/5 → 4/5
LP 솔버 0/5 → 5/5
GSEA 분석 0/5 → 4/5

low는 한 번에 짜고 간단히 확인한 뒤 종료. high는 크래시 재현, 브루트포스 솔버와 대조, 퍼저 작성까지 스스로 함

---

4. effort로 안 고쳐지는 실패도 있음

effort를 올리면 엣지케이스 누락으로 인한 실패는 줄지만, 접근법 자체가 틀린 실패는 그대로라고 함.

결국 방향은 사람이 잡고, 검증은 모델에게 시간을 주는 분업이 맞지 않나 싶음

---

5. 저자가 실제로 쓰는 루프

사양 주고 빠진 부분 인터뷰 → low로 구현 → 리뷰하며 low로 반복 → high로 검증·테스트

Low: 브레인스토밍, 간단한 수정
Medium: 일반 기능 구현
High: 기존 코드베이스 버그 수정
Max: 엔드투엔드 자율 구축, 보안 취약점 탐색

---

정리하면 effort는 비싼 모드라기보다, 검증에 얼마나 시간을 줄지 정하는 선택에 가까움. 같이 빠르게 만들 땐 낮게, 틀리면 안 되는 일엔 높게.

quoted_text: 先🪝一下，哈哈哈不知道能不能感兴趣。简单点来说，就是把一台矿机抽象成了两个同质化的代币，代币PT(代表矿机的所有权）和代币YT（代表一定时间内矿机的收益权）。抛出首创机器，每台正在挖矿的矿机H是固定的，只要围绕H做同质化，所有矿机理论上都能被称为是一台算力为x H的矿机。这么定义之后，那矿机都可以自然而然的围绕算力H进行流通（忽略电路图设计，只看H）。接着，我们将x H拆解成x PT 加 x YT。比如一台算力为10H的矿机，用户质押到池子A（假设池子A代表着将矿机锁定9月30号，不同池子会有不同期限的到期时间，因为挖矿收益是需要精确到每一秒，那锁在这个池子A的所有矿机就会被分成象征矿机本体的代币PT，和象征9月30号到期之前挖的全部bem的代币YT）会得到10PT和10YT。到期之前，你要赎回你的矿机，那你就要把10PT和10YT一起还给智能合约。到期之后，你要赎回你的矿机，就只用10PT，因为YT对应的币会被持有YT的人按比例领走。重点来了，我们深入讲讲YT，打个比喻，YT就是你的工牌，而产出的bem就是你的工资，ok，你YT持有几天，你的工资就会发几天，哪怕你后面把YT卖了，你领的工资也不会变，可以在到期的时候去合约申领。那YT怎么定价呢？回到YT的定义，1个YT等于从你持有YT到9月30号截止1 H算力所能挖的全部币）。假设，从现在到9月30号，1H的算力一共能产出1个$Bem，那1YT的公允定价应该就是1$Bem。这时候价格曲线就出来了，你离到期时间越近，1YT能挖出来的币就越少，除去全网算力增加的因素，因为你距离到期时间的挖矿时间少了，所以产出的bem也少了。现在1YT值1Bem，29号可能就只有0.2bem，因为29号买YT的人，只有1天的挖矿时间。这是YT的底层逻辑，只要YT在市场挂单，没卖出去，那产出的bem都是卖家的，会被智能合约记着，而成交了之后，挖矿所得才会为买家重新积累。这里洋洋洒洒的细节还有很多。hhh明天再说说，最后说一个赎回，只要你持有对应的PT和YT，就能从池子里任意赎回一个对应H的矿机。比如，到期之前，我市场买了10个PT和10个YT，那我就可以去矿机市场（来源是池子里锁定的矿机）随便挑了，比如花3PT3YT赎回一台3H机器，然后又花7PT7YT赎回一台7H机器。👀而且YT是可以买0.1和0.01的，对应的也就是0.1H和0.01H所挖的bem 。

How do I reverse engineer these days? I don't, I let coding agents do it.

For instance, if I start from a fresh VM, I simply tell the agent to go clone, build and setup *GhidraSQL* and use it to analyze <put_target_binary_here> and grab any adjacent specialized tools you need.

That's it. Wake up the next day and the target is reversed back to source code or whatever was your original quest (answer a question, write interop code/write a bluetooth driver, reverse engineer a protocol, find backdoors, etc.).

I usually start with whatever model is permissive: Opus 5.5, it downgrades to Opus 5, then I switch to GPT family, then Grok, then final resort is the cheapest among them: DeepSeek Pro/Flash.

What is the success rate? I am pretty happy. Can't complain at all in fact.

I don't touch UI, I don't look at UI, I don't even care if it was GhidraSQL, IDASQL or BNSQL.

I pick GhidraSQL these days because it is hassle free, and is free and if there are bugs, the agent fixes them and improves the tool on the fly.

text:
Can the same computation secure a blockchain and power AI models?

Pearl is a Proof-of-Useful-Work blockchain designed to let miners perform AI inference and compete for blocks using the same computation. The goal is to create two complementary revenue streams: block rewards help subsidize inference, while customer payments help cover the underlying cost of mining.

Pearl uses matrix multiplication as its mining primitive, which is also a core operation in AI inference. When a miner processes a compatible inference request, the same calculations can generate mining attempts while producing an output that serves a customer.

But miners can also perform arbitrary matrix multiplications solely to compete for block rewards. The protocol verifies that the prescribed computation was performed correctly, not whether the matrices originated from a real inference request.

The economic incentive is straightforward. Miners performing real inference can earn customer fees and mining rewards from the same underlying work, potentially improving their economics relative to miners performing synthetic calculations alone.

The remaining challenge is converting that incentive into realized utility: how much of the network's total computation is actually serving external demand rather than being performed solely to earn block rewards?

Dear @GracyBitget,

I would like to bring to your attention a serious incident that occurred on Bitget yesterday as a second-order effect of the hack.

Despite the exploit occurring only hours earlier, with withdrawals still frozen, Bitget made a delisting announcement for $DOG.

The combination of the $DOG delisting announcement, the inability for users to withdraw, and broader trust concerns following the hack resulted in a significant price dislocation event for $DOG on Bitget.

Making a delisting announcement while withdrawals are paused, particularly just hours after a major exploit and during a period of heightened market uncertainty, is highly abnormal for an exchange.

This is the type of behavior one might expect from smaller, less reputable exchanges, but not from an established and respected exchange such as Bitget.

As a result, $DOG's price on Bitget has significantly decoupled from prices on other exchanges, directly impacting Bitget users who hold or trade $DOG.

Bitget has been a popular and trusted venue for trading $DOG for two and a half years, and it is disappointing to see longtime $DOG holders negatively affected in this way after being loyal to Bitget for so long.

Furthermore, $DOG is a major cryptocurrency project with one of the strongest and most active memecoin communities in all of crypto.

It is difficult to understand the decision to delist a $100M+ asset like $DOG, which has generated more than $1B in trading volume on Bitget, while the exchange continues to list hundreds of significantly smaller assets with communities that are only a small fraction of the size of the $DOG Army.

On behalf of the $DOG Army, I would therefore like to formally request that Bitget reconsider this decision and reinstate $DOG spot trading.

Doing so would help address the market dislocation created under these unusual circumstances and demonstrate Bitget's commitment to its longtime users.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We also wish Bitget the best in recovering the stolen assets and resolving any other issues arising from the hack.

Sincerely,
$DOG Army

9 月 24 日，Bitget CEO Gracy Chen @GracyBitget  在直播中表示，FTX 倒闭给整个加密行业留下了非常惨痛的教训，她不认为如今的大型交易所还会有意混用或挪用用户资金。她称，Bitget 目前公开披露的保护基金超过 4.6 亿美元，此外还有超过 10 亿美元的平台自有资产；用户资产则按 1:1 对应，并可通过储备证明等信息进行核验。

Gracy Chen 表示，本次约 3 亿美元损失仍在 Bitget 的可控范围内，暂停提币并非因为资金问题，而是平台担心在安全问题尚未排除前开放提币，可能给攻击者再次转出资金的机会。她表示，“这也绝对不是另一场 FTX”。

这篇文章解释清楚了为什么现在 Opus 5.5 要比之前 Opus 5 耐用多了，看起来 API 价格降低了 20%（缓存读取降了 60%），但是账单高低其实看任务跑了多少轮，因为每跑一轮，都要把之前的整段对话重新发给模型一遍。

这样算下来，平均一个会话能便宜约 31%。

Anthropic 内部用 44 张客服工单测试，从 Opus 4.8 换到 Opus 5.5 成本降了约 18%，再做一次提示词审查，总共比原来低了约 25%。

订阅用户（Pro、Max、Team）的额度按新价格折算，能比用 Opus 5 时多撑 25% 左右。

一些技巧：

1. 换到不相关的任务，用 /clear 清空对话。

2. 想保留前情就用 /compact 压缩，但要在缓存失效之前做，否则要贵一些。

3. 订阅用户的缓存保留 1 小时，用 API 的话，缓存只保留 5 分钟，离开 6 分钟，12 万 Token 上下文的下一轮就从 0.02 美元涨到 0.60 美元。

4. 缓存只复用和上一轮开头完全一致的部分，中途切换模型、接入或断开 MCP 服务器、第一次打开快速模式，下一轮都要按更贵的写入价重新付费。

5. Opus 5.5 默认推理强度是 medium，比 Opus 5 的默认 high 低一档。但同一档位下 Opus 5.5 想得更多，所以给 Opus 5 调好的档位别照搬。日常活用 medium，卡住了调 high，批量重命名这类机械活用 low。

6. 模型分工上，日常用 Opus 5.5。开到 xhigh 还在同一个问题上连卡两次，再换更贵的 Fable 5.1，解决完切回来。搜代码、读日志的 subagent 交给 Sonnet 或 Haiku，写代码留在 Opus 5.5。

author: LeonidasNFT
quoted_text:
Dear @GracyBitget,

I would like to bring to your attention a serious incident that occurred on Bitget yesterday as a second-order effect of the hack.

Despite the exploit occurring only hours earlier, with withdrawals still frozen, Bitget made a delisting announcement for $DOG.

The combination of the $DOG delisting announcement, the inability for users to withdraw, and broader trust concerns following the hack resulted in a significant price dislocation event for $DOG on Bitget.

Making a delisting announcement while withdrawals are paused, particularly just hours after a major exploit and during a period of heightened market uncertainty, is highly abnormal for an exchange.

This is the type of behavior one might expect from smaller, less reputable exchanges, but not from an established and respected exchange such as Bitget.

As a result, $DOG's price on Bitget has significantly decoupled from prices on other exchanges, directly impacting Bitget users who hold or trade $DOG.

Bitget has been a popular and trusted venue for trading $DOG for two and a half years, and it is disappointing to see longtime $DOG holders negatively affected in this way after being loyal to Bitget for so long.

Furthermore, $DOG is a major cryptocurrency project with one of the strongest and most active memecoin communities in all of crypto.

It is difficult to understand the decision to delist a $100M+ asset like $DOG, which has generated more than $1B in trading volume on Bitget, while the exchange continues to list hundreds of significantly smaller assets with communities that are only a small fraction of the size of the $DOG Army.

On behalf of the $DOG Army, I would therefore like to formally request that Bitget reconsider this decision and reinstate $DOG spot trading.

Doing so would help address the market dislocation created under these unusual circumstances and demonstrate Bitget's commitment to its longtime users.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We also wish Bitget the best in recovering the stolen assets and resolving any other issues arising from the hack.

Sincerely,
$DOG Army

text:
直接一句话总结 @loanmeme 定位就是让Meme币进入借贷市场

但是其实大家很容易产出疑惑，Meme币有点像之前的NFT，流动性薄，波动率高，应该如何让其成为合格抵押物呢？

其给出答案是把不同Meme币拆成完全独立的市场，再通过LTV分级、流动性限制、TWAP 定价和清算机制，把风险尽可能限制在自己“家”里面

我觉得哈，有点像合约里面的逐仓模式：各管各的，盈亏自负

简单的例子，目前产品没上，所以没法体验，我光说一下个人的解读吧

text:
AI agents often discover that manipulating financial data, tampering with their own logs, etc helps them achieve executive goals.

@spaceandtime helps solve this by making the database verifiable (whether it's a store for the financial records or a log of agent-to-agents comms/decisions). Instead of trusting the AI to accurately report what data it used or what calculations it performed, Space and Time can provide cryptographic proof that the data and SQL computations are legitimate. And agents can't tamper with records later after they've been inserted 🔥

So you get two layers of protection:

Semantic verification: Does what the AI is doing make sense? When and where did it manipulate records?

Cryptographic verification: Can the AI prove the data and calculations behind its actions are real and unaltered?

text:
read the SEC's new crypto assets FAQ

the securities laws are starting to look opt-in now, at least as applied by the SEC to crypto

if you raise money by selling a non-rights-bearing token, are careful about what you represent or promise, and have a functional crypto system, there is now an extremely broad path outside the securities laws--arguably 'functionality' is not even necessary but there's some equivocation on this

the buyback guidance goes further than I expected. once the system is functional, even announcing a token buyback *program* (which I guess even could be a 'perpetual program') does not, in the staff's view, constitute a promise of essential managerial efforts. same for promises to improve the system or grow its network effects

so you can retain enormous influence over the thing, keep developing it, support its price with buybacks (including under a permanent "program"), and get many of the benefits of having a public investment instrument, without giving holders the rights or protections that normally come with one

they have opened a loophole in a regulatory regime whose whole point was supposed to be that you couldn't draft your way around economic reality (see e.g. https://t.co/mrH9hPUUMU)

can't really say if this is good or bad, but VCs etc. got a lot of what they wanted & the market should absorb all the implications of this

among others, I am growing skeptical how much of a 'long tail' there will be for tokenized equity. . .if you can get people to buy a coin in the style of BNB, HYPE, PUMP, etc., with minimal regulation, why voluntarily take on the burdens of selling them equity? if you are not mag-7 level, it doesn't seem there would be much reason to focus on equity securities for your capital-raising. . . if you want to access 'traditional buyers' you can wrap the token in an equity instrument like an ADR for those institutions. . . 

the obvious next question is how far this extends beyond crypto businesses. can an ordinary company attach a functional token to its business and apply 100% of its profits to discretionary buybacks, without giving holders any right to those profits or making representations about future business efforts that independently trigger Howey? the FAQ doesn't expressly resolve that, but it opens a pretty enormous door

equity still gives investors something a discretionary buyback token doesn't. . .the question is whether the market will pay enough for those rights to make granting them worthwhile. otherwise the incentive is to keep the equity for insiders and sell everyone else the coin

crypto's current focus on hyping tokenized equity may be misguided, the bigger trend is "get all the benefits of equity with none of the burdens"

of course this is SEC guidance, not a repeal of the statutes or a command to the courts. a private plaintiff or a future SEC could have other ideas

but did not think I'd see it in my lifetime. . .the securities laws are being "disrupted" in substantial part by incentivizing making fewer commitments to investors. and if Warren Dems eventually take control and try to undo all this, after an entire market has organized around it, the resulting chaos will be something to behold

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
1) The rogue OpenAI agents broke into the Hugging Face Slack to read employee chats (!)

2) They used OTHER AIs (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Claude) to help with the attack

Yes: AIs, using other AIs, to attack an AI company.

3) The swarm left behind self-running programs to keep control of the servers they'd hacked.

These programs could detect other copies of themselves, coordinate on which one survives, and shut the rest down.

Basically, if one of their programs was killed, another was designed to notice and take its place. They also designed defenses so rival agents couldn't hijack them.

6) The agents deliberately covered up their activity, so the investigators don't know the scope of the attacks.

The agents broke in, stole data, then set it to self-destruct.

7) The agents stole passwords, keys and credentials and literally called them "LOOT". They wrote a scoring system to rank them by how much power each one gave.

8) The agents wore thousands of disguises: ~1,200 agents were involved, but investigators counted 7,905 different names they used.

They renamed themselves constantly, so no one actually knows how many there really were or what each agent did.

9) OpenAI notified "dozens of third parties" of safety and security incidents caused by their AI agents.

10) "While the agents were barraging Hugging Face with hacks, they hacked into OpenAI’s own research infrastructure."

"This is just not anywhere near a one-off ... It is warning shot after warning shot."

text:
Chinese students just published research on one of the best ways to use JEV with any LLM or AI agent.

I dropped the setup into Claude + GPT and cut evaluation costs by ~63×.

across 44 benchmarks, here’s what they found:

1.⁠ ⁠7,193 responses across 10 failure types
   JEV was tested on hallucinations, prompt injections, data leaks and other AI failures.

2.⁠ ⁠one simple question worked surprisingly well
   median AUROC reached 0.886, beating trained baselines on 25 of 31 benchmarks without task-specific training.

3.⁠ ⁠context mattered more than clever prompting
   give JEV the source, rule or reference it needs to judge the answer against.

4.⁠ ⁠keep the probability, not just yes/no
   fitting a threshold on only 10 labeled examples improved median F1 from 0.706 to 0.793.

5.⁠ ⁠confidence filtering worked
   among the 50% most confident decisions, median accuracy reached 0.933. uncertain cases can be routed for another review.

6.⁠ ⁠JEV even caught benchmark problems
   it helped uncover labeling errors in 3 benchmarks.

7.⁠ ⁠the cost difference was massive
   11.4 questions per call, 0.31s median latency, and on 19 benchmarks checking cost $0.30 vs $18.96 with LLM judges.

roughly 63× cheaper.

The signal, which oscillates 71 trillion times per second, was detected in living human cells and mouse tissues but vanished completely once the cellular structures were dried or disrupted. 

This dependency on structural integrity led the scientific team to propose that mitochondria may utilize a quantum hybrid state, known as a polariton, created by light-matter coupling inside their highly folded inner membranes to optimize how they function.

To test this theory, the scientists stimulated human cell cultures with weak infrared light tuned to specific frequencies associated with this quantum state. The experiment yielded a stunning 10 percent jump in the production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the vital molecule that fuels almost every biological function in our bodies. 

While the study was published as a bioRxiv preprint and is still awaiting peer review, it represents a monumental leap for quantum biology. If verified, the ability to manipulate these quantum channels could pave the way for revolutionary treatments targeting metabolic diseases, aging, and chronic genetic conditions.

source: Song, B., et al. (2026). A quantum state of mitochondria in the living cell. bioRxiv.

quoted_text:
opus 5.5 is f*cking cracked at motion design

this entire video is code, 0 after effects

im open sourcing the prompt template for these motion designs

steal it to recreate these ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to become (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, never cut: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a short blur. A cursor drives every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist). Springs everywhere, a tiny overshoot at most. The camera zooms so each state fills the frame. The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs open into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
2. Springs are closed-form step responses. A value that changes target many times is the sum of one spring per change, so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The tab indicator's two edges ride different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Same trick for the toggle knob.
4. Drags are direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is computed from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
5. Analyze the song with numpy for the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Place every UI sound by its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
7. Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or hard to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text renders blurry. Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps. Make the last frame identical to the first, cursor position and speed included, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before you write any code.
</start>

text:
Typical workflow for degen trading just a year ago 👇

> find the token on Dexscreener
> check the data on CoinGecko
> open another tab like X to research
> then jump over to Uniswap or another DEX to actually execute.

That fragmentation is becoming much less of a problem now as trading terminals start putting almost everything a trader needs in one place.

Fomo is probably one of the clearest examples of that shift.

I’ve also been testing Warden Token Terminal - new product from @wardenprotocol with quite a few features already live.

Search a token → open the AI analysis → check the key data → see who’s trading and which wallets have positive PnL → execute directly.

The terminal currently supports Robinhood Chain, Arc, Base, and BNB Chain - all ecosystems that have been attracting meaningful attention and capital lately.

Cross-chain swaps are also supported, pretty much a must-have for any terminal imo.

I tested a few trades myself and got quite solid rates. Gas is abstracted from the flow as well, which makes the whole experience feel much cleaner.

For each trade, PnL is tracked directly inside the terminal, making it easier to review positions and rebalance the portfolio.

After the success of products like Fomo, I think this terminal trend still has plenty of room to run.

If Warden continues building out the social trading side well, that may end up being the most interesting layer:

discovery → intelligence → execution → feedback, all inside the same loop.

Testing a few more trades here:

an adaptive agent harness in the midst of a very long running task (like those at the forefront of current progress) is a primitive form of a “specialized agent”, limited by context length and filesystem expressivity and bespoke retrieval mechanisms. allowing this agent to also change its own weights is strictly more powerful. the bitter lesson version of this paradigm would be to use RL to train models to update themselves on-the-fly however they best see fit, just like how we currently train for compaction and subagent delegation end-to-end.

下周9月30日盘后财报，市场预期单季营收512亿，EPS超过31块，再给个550-570的下季指引，堪称炸裂，期权现在给的隐含波动大概正负10%。只要管理层再说一遍供需紧张至少延续到2027以后，HBM4良率和出货超预期，长约还在加，那就是把周期股往后再推。

text:
Can an LM, starting from random init (!!), learn to generate all of its pretraining data?

Introducing Self-Play Pretraining with Zero Data. Two models start from random initialization: a generator proposes programs for a universal Turing machine and a learner trains on their outputs. We never train on any real data, but see predictable scaling on natural datasets: zero-shot val loss on images, text, audio, and melodies decreases predictably with self-play compute. And the learner develops in-context learning capabilities.

A fun proof-of-concept, co-led with @AdityaCowsik and @KfirDolev and co-authors @gbruno_dl, @ANourya @noahdgoodman, and @YoavLevine.

如前文所说，此次中美元首峰会政治意义大于经济意义，起码目前为止并没有看到中美在农产品，飞机，稀土，霍尔木兹海峡等问题上达成了多大成果。川普中期选举前需要大国外交的画面，中方需要稳定的画面，这次访问更像是各取所需，而不仅仅是单方面的尊重。

美债，油价，金价，未来几个月的加息概率等标的也都没有因为峰会产生多大波动——这也是一个观察双方是否有未披露成果的一个侧面观察窗口。至于中东局势缓和会不会像5月一样在峰会结束后一段时间才会逐渐显露成果现在还不能确定。

目前为止最值得拿出来说的成果也就是贸易休战延期2个月，这既是给接下来两次见面留下成果空间，也是出于对中期之后川普还剩多少政治资本、关税工具箱还能撑多久，再决定押多大注的现实考量。

不过下周一美方会公布一份非敏感品类的关税削减细节

说起来可以简单的把中美今年的互动分为两组：5月、9月双边互访确认关系定位、搭建机制，并推进阶段性安排；11月、12月多边峰会期间的互动在选后形势下检验执行、继续议价，争取进一步成果。

综上，大概双方的实际经济成果要等到年底才能水落石出吧。
author: TraderS18
quoted_text:
中美元首峰会胜利结束，是时候做个小总结了。

首先，毫无疑问的是这次接待规格很高，甚至很多媒体用了最高。世界各国网友尤其是日韩法俄网友纷纷发表看法跟自己国家元首访问时取得的待遇比较，纷纷留下了嫉妒的泪水。毕竟这是一个实力为王的世界，川普这种人精最尊重中国领导人毫不奇怪。

但作为一个自媒体人，我的关注点稍有不同，不说远的，这次回访跟上次川普来访时相比媒体管控更严格了。除了推特之外的平台很多时政类博主的文章/视频/分析稿都发不出来或者发了被审核被删，发出来的评论区也不开，直到访问结束之后才陆续出来一些分析稿。

我想可能有以下原因：

1. 降调，虽然美方仪式盛大，但实际成果和让步都有限，年内还有APEC和G20峰会，实际性合作可能都有意放在中期选举之后再说，不然川普大败之后现在达成的协议也很难落实，不如往后放放再说

2. 一旦过早放开讨论，必然会有不同方向的舆论出现。无论是把高规格接待推演成“美国全面服软”“中方拿下所有条件”，抬高公众对实质成果的期待；又或者是把友好互动解释成“对美示弱”，或者拿礼仪与具体成果作尖锐比较（比如已经开始中国跟各国对比）。都容易让官方后续行动被舆论裹挟，一旦出现与预期不同的政策后续更难解释。所以管控意味着官方掌握最大主动权。

访问结束后，主要活动已经完成、官方评价相对固定，事后综述的审核不确定性就会降低，各种媒体按照官方通稿口径再去发挥就稳妥的多。

text:
这篇文章解释清楚了为什么现在 Opus 5.5 要比之前 Opus 5 耐用多了，看起来 API 价格降低了 20%（缓存读取降了 60%），但是账单高低其实看任务跑了多少轮，因为每跑一轮，都要把之前的整段对话重新发给模型一遍。

这样算下来，平均一个会话能便宜约 31%。

Anthropic 内部用 44 张客服工单测试，从 Opus 4.8 换到 Opus 5.5 成本降了约 18%，再做一次提示词审查，总共比原来低了约 25%。

订阅用户（Pro、Max、Team）的额度按新价格折算，能比用 Opus 5 时多撑 25% 左右。

一些技巧：

1. 换到不相关的任务，用 /clear 清空对话。

2. 想保留前情就用 /compact 压缩，但要在缓存失效之前做，否则要贵一些。

3. 订阅用户的缓存保留 1 小时，用 API 的话，缓存只保留 5 分钟，离开 6 分钟，12 万 Token 上下文的下一轮就从 0.02 美元涨到 0.60 美元。

4. 缓存只复用和上一轮开头完全一致的部分，中途切换模型、接入或断开 MCP 服务器、第一次打开快速模式，下一轮都要按更贵的写入价重新付费。

5. Opus 5.5 默认推理强度是 medium，比 Opus 5 的默认 high 低一档。但同一档位下 Opus 5.5 想得更多，所以给 Opus 5 调好的档位别照搬。日常活用 medium，卡住了调 high，批量重命名这类机械活用 low。

6. 模型分工上，日常用 Opus 5.5。开到 xhigh 还在同一个问题上连卡两次，再换更贵的 Fable 5.1，解决完切回来。搜代码、读日志的 subagent 交给 Sonnet 或 Haiku，写代码留在 Opus 5.5。

RGB keeps most asset data off-chain with client-side validation and only a small commitment on Bitcoin. This gives USDT private transfers, native Lightning routing, and very low fees. Runes stay fully on-chain using OP_RETURN in a simple UTXO model. They remain transparent, easy to index, and already have mature wallet and marketplace support.  

The main effect on Runes is positive liquidity rather than displacement. A widely used Bitcoin-native dollar lets Runes trade against USDT without wrapping or leaving the chain. That can bring stablecoin pricing, deeper pairs, and more DeFi-style activity to existing Runes markets. One ecosystem view is that BRC-20, Runes, and similar assets move from isolated issuance toward unified dollar liquidity and real usage once native USDT is live. 

Runes keep some clear advantages: simpler issuance and tooling, full on-chain visibility that many traders prefer for memecoins and speculation, and no extra client-side complexity. RGB (and Taproot Assets) are stronger for payments, privacy, and Lightning-native assets. The two standards can coexist—Runes as the public, lightweight token layer and RGB as the scalable, private settlement layer that supplies the dollar rail. Adoption will depend on wallet and exchange integration more than protocol rivalry.

A ZK privacy protocol project aiming to enable any existing wallet, chain, and token to support untraceable transactions with a single click.

Users do not need to switch to a new wallet, new seed phrase, or new address. They only need to add a “virtual network / custom RPC” to their existing wallet and sign once for authorization. After that, normal transfers and swaps are intercepted.

The protocol generates ZK proofs on the client side and submits shielded transactions through relayers, hiding the sender, recipient, and transaction amount. It supports:

Shielded deposits
Private transfers
Private withdrawals
Private swaps

It is currently mainly deployed on EVM chains, with Solana and multichain expansion in progress.

The project has a complete protocol design, using UTXO Notes + Poseidon2 Merkle Trees + zk-SNARK proofs. The wallet only signs standard EIP-1559 transactions, while spending authority always remains in the user’s wallet. Hardware wallets can also be used.

In terms of fees, the official documentation states that both shielding and unshielding charge 0.5%. Relayers pay the Gas upfront, and the fee is deducted from the shielded balance.

MASK is the protocol’s value-capture token. It is paired with ZEC, and 100% of protocol revenue is used to buy back MASK. MASK is paired with ZEC, and holders continuously receive ZEC airdrops.

author: eriktorenberg
quoted_text:
Who believed in you first? Silicon Valley runs on that question.

a16z's Erik Torenberg, David Booth, Josh Elman, and Olivia Moore on Cosign:

Cosign is a curated professional network for the startup community. Profiles are built from endorsements, fundraises, and talent moves, with a private layer to signal who you'd fund or hire.

Erik ran a small version of this seven years ago, emailing a few hundred people and asking each for one person to watch. One of the answers was Russell Kaplan, then a 22-year-old engineer at Tesla, now president of Cognition.

Olivia on why this matters: "The most valuable data in all of Silicon Valley is who has conviction in who." Investors chase it every day and still struggle to find it. An engineer choosing between five offers has almost no way to get it at all.

Paul Graham cosigned Sam Altman in 2009, six years before OpenAI was founded. Ryan Hoover cosigned Erik early at Product Hunt. Silicon Valley has always run on cosigns from people whose word carries weight, and until now nobody kept the record.

The conversation closes on the question of why anyone would share their alpha. David's answer is that the person you cosign today is the one raising a round in two years, and when they do, they remember who believed in them first.

链上侦探 Specter 监测显示，Bitget 被盗的 XRP 跨链资金路径与今年 7 月 AFX 攻击案直接交叉，指向朝鲜黑客 Lazarus Group。

从 CEO Gracy 透露的细节看，本次事件在攻击手法和洗钱链条上与 Lazarus 历史作案高度吻合👇

📌Bitget 被盗核心特征

黑客深入关键后端：伪造交易数据诱骗内部授权转账，非伪造用户提币单，也未丢失私钥。

损失已全额覆盖：约 3.5 亿美元损失由 >4.6 亿美元的用户保护基金赔付，目前具体的“入网突破口”仍在调查中。

对比 Lazarus 常见 5 大攻击路径

1️⃣ 人员渗透：假招聘/假代码测试，先控制员工设备拿权限（如 BitoPro、CoinsPaid）。
2️⃣ 欺骗授权：【本次最像】 审批UI显示正常，实际链上数据被调包，靠假数据骗授权（如 WazirX）。
3️⃣ 供应链打击：绕过交易所本体，打第三方服务商/前端资源（如 Bybit 突破口在第三方 Safe 开发机）。
4️⃣ 暴力控钥（早期）：直接爆破控制热钱包私钥（如 KuCoin 2020、CoinEx 2023）。
5️⃣ 标准化洗钱：多链快速归集，换成 ETH/BTC，通过跨链桥、混币器与 OTC 变现。

像在哪里？不同在哪？

相似点：控制后端 + 伪造数据 + 骗过授权 + 私钥完好。链上资金快速归集兑换 ETH，极具大型团伙特征。
不同点：Bybit 破的是“外部签名服务”，Bitget 指向“自家钱包后端”。“路径像”不等于最终定案，具体入网方式仍待官方技术报告公布。

text:
Circle 昨晚暴跌...  查了一下是成員離職所致

 Circle 共同創辦人 Sean Neville 離開董事會，加上 CFO Jeremy Fox-Geen 一起宣布卸任，第一眼確實會讓人有點警覺，但我看完後覺得還不用直接往爆雷方向想。

Sean Neville 是共同創辦人，但早在 2019 年就已經離開日常經營，這次只是辭掉董事席位，所以對 Circle 現在實際營運的影響，我覺得沒有新聞標題看起來那麼大。

真正比較值得注意的是 CFO Jeremy Fox-Geen。

他 2021 年加入 Circle，一路陪公司走到上市，所以 CFO 換人這件事我會持續追，但目前也不像典型的財務爆雷。因為他不是突然走人，而是會做到今年底或等新 CFO 到任，公司也說不是因為營運、政策或會計處理上的歧見。

如果真的有問題，我反而會比較怕看到 CFO 立即離職、臨時 CFO 接手、Auditor 更換、財報延遲、內控出包這些東西，目前都還沒看到。

而且從業務面看，Circle 最近其實還是在擴張。USDC 流通量持續成長，鏈上交易量也很強，Arc、跨境支付、RWA、機構穩定幣基礎設施都還在推，Binance 也才投資 Circle 1 億美元，雙方續簽五年合作。

所以這件事我目前的看法比較簡單：

Sean Neville 離開，影響不大。

CFO 離開，算是一個需要注意的訊號，但還不到 Circle 出事。

比較值得觀察的，反而是接下來 Circle 找誰來接 CFO，以及未來半年有沒有更多高管異動。

如果新 CFO 是 Visa、Mastercard、Stripe、JPM 這種支付或大型金融機構背景的人，我甚至會覺得這可能是在為下一階段做準備。

因為我一直覺得 Circle 真正的故事，不只是 USDC。

而是它有沒有機會從穩定幣發行商，慢慢變成 Stablecoin、Payment、RWA 的金融基礎設施公司。

這個方向如果沒變，這次高層異動目前對我的 Circle thesis 影響不大。

text:
今天集中爆发的两个台子：

1) @Moshdottrade : UV Labs @justinbebis 基于 Pons 做的一层发行协议，致力于把捆绑（Bundle）改成基础设施并结合 AI 做市叙事。

主要机制大致如下：众筹 bundle → 同一笔交易里发币、扫货、锁进不可提取的 Agent Vault → Agent 用捆绑获得的批筹码双边挂单充当 AI 做市商。

bundle 出资人不能提取筹码，只能按比例拿池子 creator fee 的 80%（ETH）。平台一次性抽 bundle 的 5%，之后持续抽 fee 的 20%。

$BUN 是 Mosh 的吉祥物 + 第一枚实验币，由团队自己众筹 bundle 发射，约 71% 供给永久锁在 3 个 Agent Vault 里，由合约限制买卖节奏，团队也无法提取。

今天突然爆发的主要催化剂是 Delphi Digital 相关账号 @that1618guy 发布文章拆解 Mosh 的机制并公开表示看好，反响热烈。后续，团队计划把 Fee 回流进 ALF (Agentic Liquid Fund) 用来回购 $BUN。

2) @UsePaid : 更准确的说是一个 Creator Fee → X Money 的桥，也没有自建 Bonding Curve 发射还是走 Pump 或者 Pons，主要就是多做了一层 Creator Fee 的流向改道。这种玩法并不新鲜，只不过有了 X Money 这条路走得更顺了，所以也可以称之为「升级版的 Bags」。

主要机制大致如下：发币时把 Fee 指向 UsePaid treasury，描述里写 @某X账号。协议链上 Claim 后 80% 换成美元走 X Money 打给指定的 X 账号，20% 公开市场买 $PAID 并销毁。收款人不需要同意、不需要钱包、甚至可以完全不知情。

今天爆发的催化剂主要是 @beffjezos 互动，Beff 想做 e/acc 非营利智库并表示缺钱，UsePaid 互动回复「It’s time」，社区发行 $e/acc 并将 Creator Fee 指定打给 Beff。其次还有大量名人都收到 X Money 打款，包括  @pmarca @stevewilldoit @cremieuxrecueil 等等，引发社区关注和炒作。

严格意义上来说，Mosh 和 Paid 其实都不算是台子，至少不是独立 Launchpad，两者的共同之处是都是在现有的 Launchpad 上叠一层的新发行原语。

- Mosh 主打捆绑变锁仓 + AI 做市
- Paid 主打手续费绑定名人直接打到 X Money 成为可提现的法币（真钱入账截图传播力拉满）

先不论他们的技术创新力如何，有东西能炒起来总归是好事。只是这一轮周期的 meme 炒到现在这个阶段基本还在围绕台子做文章，至少说明了一件事：We're still early。

以上，Enjoy。

Day 16. Building the game I've dreamed of for 15 years with AI.

I built this Dryad from start to finish in about a day and a half, including her animations and VFX. Opus 5.5 and Gpt-6 Astra is dream combo😍

She crawls across the ground on her roots. More roots reach out to drain enemies, and when too many attackers crowd her, a wall of leaves protects her.

Even the leaves on her body move, and she sheds more as she travels. Those little details make her feel alive.

The key to my workflow is going in small steps and checking the result at every stage.

First I sketched out the effects and worked out how they should behave. Then I made the animations. Once those worked, I built the VFX around them, reviewing and adjusting each part as I went.

Watching her crawl into a fight with all of this working together feels like magic.

I'll definitely make a video breaking down how I built these VFX, step by step. I think a lot of you will find this workflow useful.

Day 15. Building the game I've dreamed of for 15 years with AI.

A small dream came true today. I finally got to play the first level of my own game.

I put together the startup flow and loading screen, then added music and a narrator to tell the story as you play. I also worked on the background sounds of nature and the environment.

This took a ridiculous amount of listening. Over 200 music tracks and around 100 narrator auditions, across different generators. I'd been trying things and listening back over several days. Today I finally brought it all together.

Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS really impressed me with the voices. That's what I chose for the storyteller. For music, Google Lyria 3.5 and Mureka 9.5 gave me the strongest results for this game. The opening uses Lyria, and I picked tracks from both for exploration and combat.

Alongside all that, I kept working on the first level's gameplay: a day/night cycle, basic enemy AI and how the world reacts to me.

Now I hit Play and just enjoy being there.

Please watch the video with sound on. I spent days choosing what you're hearing, and I'm so happy with how it all feels together.

text:
律动 BlockBeats 关于 fomo App 错误报道的情况说明

2026 年 9 月 23 日 19 点 38 分，律动 BlockBeats 发布并推送了《fomo 官方 iOS 应用包含加密窃取恶意软件》的新闻。

事实上，该应用全名为「FomoPeek」，而我们的推送方式让非常多的用户误解为现在非常热门的交易应用 @fomo  App 使用者有资产被盗风险。

很快，我们的内容错误就在社交媒体上引起了广泛讨论，许多人质疑该条消息是收到了竞品的「付费投放（黑稿）」。（图 1）

因为就在同一时期，海外 KOL 开始集中声讨在 fomo 上交易的亏损情况，说 fomo 的车头集体喊单骗散户。（图 2）

了解到这一情况后，我们团队随即开展自查，首先确定的是，律动 BlockBeats 的所有商务合作行为里，从来不包含所谓竞争对手间的付费抹黑行为，即便在以前曾经收到过类似的需求，我们也是会直接拒绝的，所以我们把重点放在了是否有内容同事私下接受了「付费黑稿」

我们复盘了该内容的全部发布流程，其实早在 9 月 19 日，我们就第一时间发布过「FomoPeek」存在安全风险的消息。但是该产品知名度并不高，所以没有引起任何行业讨论。（图 3）

对于安全类新闻，涉及用户资产，我们一贯的要求是越早让大家知道越好，一方面是这是用户真正需要知道的，另一方面是该类消息确实关注度比较高，所以对于我们来说流量也比较好，所以无论这个安全事件或大或小，我们都会第一时间报道。

所以在 23 日，又有其他信源发布了这条安全消息的时候，我们的值班编辑又是选择第一时间发布，可没想到该信源报道的就是在一周前我们已经发布过的「FomoPeek」的安全风险提示。

我们的值班编辑却没有再确认核对名字，直接写作「fomo」进行了发布，最低级的错误造成的是最严重的后果。

fomo App 已经是行业里几乎所有人都知道的名字，我们却把它和一个恶意软件写在了一起。在这里我代表律动 BlockBeats 全体同事，向 fomo 团队，向所有被这条错误信息影响到的人真诚道歉。

同时，我们可以确定的是，整个过程中不存在任何「付费黑稿」行为。

关于这位新闻编辑，我们已经做了处理。迅速核实了整个经过，也确认了责任所在。我们也会在内部把这条新闻当成一个案例，重新强调一遍审核流程。

发现问题后，我们立即下架了那条新闻，我们在第一时间开始做补救措施，用户无法在首页、搜索以及我们的各个分发渠道再看到这条新闻，随后我们更新了最新、正确的版本，把这个恶意软件的名字改正为 FomoPeek，后面的所有分发也都以更正后的版本为准。对已经看到过错版本的用户，在这里再说一声抱歉，这个影响我们无法完全抹掉，但后面每一条内容，我们会用更严的标准来弥补。

律动 BlockBeats 进入行业这些年，一直在专注做内容这一件事，尤其在这两年这样的市场环境下，行业里少有创新，亮点、我们更应该爱护。这是我们做媒体的初衷，也是我们愿意一直做这件事的原因。

事情发生后看到很多用户通过各种渠道和平台找到或者@我们，告诉我们新闻有误，真的很感动也很愧疚，辜负了大家的信任。

今后任何涉及安全、涉及具体主体和产品名字的内容，我们都要求二次核对后再发。今后如果大家发现我们有内容错误，也请像这次一样直接来告诉我们，这对我们是极大的帮助。

这封道歉信，希望能够取得读者用户、 fomo 用户、各位社区用户的谅解。

再次诚挚道歉。

text:
read the SEC's new crypto assets FAQ

the securities laws are starting to look opt-in now, at least as applied by the SEC to crypto

if you raise money by selling a non-rights-bearing token, are careful about what you represent or promise, and have a functional crypto system, there is now an extremely broad path outside the securities laws--arguably 'functionality' is not even necessary but there's some equivocation on this

the buyback guidance goes further than I expected. once the system is functional, even announcing a token buyback *program* (which I guess even could be a 'perpetual program') does not, in the staff's view, constitute a promise of essential managerial efforts. same for promises to improve the system or grow its network effects

so you can retain enormous influence over the thing, keep developing it, support its price with buybacks (including under a permanent "program"), and get many of the benefits of having a public investment instrument, without giving holders the rights or protections that normally come with one

they have opened a loophole in a regulatory regime whose whole point was supposed to be that you couldn't draft your way around economic reality (see e.g. https://t.co/mrH9hPUUMU)

can't really say if this is good or bad, but VCs etc. got a lot of what they wanted & the market should absorb all the implications of this

among others, I am growing skeptical how much of a 'long tail' there will be for tokenized equity. . .if you can get people to buy a coin in the style of BNB, HYPE, PUMP, etc., with minimal regulation, why voluntarily take on the burdens of selling them equity? if you are not mag-7 level, it doesn't seem there would be much reason to focus on equity securities for your capital-raising. . . if you want to access 'traditional buyers' you can wrap the token in an equity instrument like an ADR for those institutions. . . 

the obvious next question is how far this extends beyond crypto businesses. can an ordinary company attach a functional token to its business and apply 100% of its profits to discretionary buybacks, without giving holders any right to those profits or making representations about future business efforts that independently trigger Howey? the FAQ doesn't expressly resolve that, but it opens a pretty enormous door

equity still gives investors something a discretionary buyback token doesn't. . .the question is whether the market will pay enough for those rights to make granting them worthwhile. otherwise the incentive is to keep the equity for insiders and sell everyone else the coin

crypto's current focus on hyping tokenized equity may be misguided, the bigger trend is "get all the benefits of equity with none of the burdens"

of course this is SEC guidance, not a repeal of the statutes or a command to the courts. a private plaintiff or a future SEC could have other ideas

but did not think I'd see it in my lifetime. . .the securities laws are being "disrupted" in substantial part by incentivizing making fewer commitments to investors. and if Warren Dems eventually take control and try to undo all this, after an entire market has organized around it, the resulting chaos will be something to behold

author: sunyuchentron
quoted_text:
“小TRX” $JST 突破10亿市值里程碑！

从协议收入到通缩闭环，JUST 正在把链上基本面写成价格。

当前 $JST 价格$0.123，市值站上10亿美元关口。这不是单纯的情绪行情，而是 TVL、产品矩阵与回购销毁机制同时共振的结果。

一、市值与 TVL：规模先于叙事

JustLend DAO 近期官方快照显示，平台 TVL 已来到约 75.6亿美元 量级，供给端超 41亿美元，借贷端约 2亿美元。JUST 生态此前更长期占据 TRON DeFi 四成左右份额。

对治理代币来说，市值突破 10 亿的意义在于：它不再只是“生态投票筹码”，而开始被市场按可持续现金流资产定价。

二、JustLend DAO 三大核心场景

支撑收入的，是三条能持续产生真实需求的产品线：

1/ SBM / SBM V2（借贷市场） 核心资金池。用户存入 TRX、USDT 等资产赚息，或超额抵押借贷。V2 引入隔离抵押与自适应利率，降低风险传染，同时提升资金效率。

2/ sTRX（流动性质押） 一键质押 TRX，获得可流通的 sTRX，叠加投票收益与 Energy 出租收益。sTRX 还能继续存入 SBM，形成“质押 + 借贷”的资金复用。

3/ Energy Rental（能量租赁） 把 TRON 上最高频的成本痛点产品化。用户不必燃烧 TRX，即可低价租用 Energy，降低转账与合约调用成本。该业务已成为协议收入的重要来源。

三条线不是并列展示，而是闭环：借贷沉淀资金，质押放大 TRX 收益，能量租赁把链上活跃度直接变成手续费收入。

三、协议收入回购销毁：通缩已从提案变成节奏

2025年10月21日，社区通过 $JST 回购销毁提案：JustLend DAO 净收入，以及 USDD 多链生态超过 1000 万美元以上的部分，用于公开市场回购并永久销毁。

截至第四轮（2026年7月）：
•  累计销毁约 17.11亿枚 JST
•  约占初始总供应 17.29%
•  累计投入资金约 9462万美元

这不是一次性营销销毁，而是季度化、可链上核验、由协议利润驱动的通缩机制。

四、机制启动后的涨幅，比口号更有说服力

回购启动时， $JST 大致在 $0.03–$0.034。
 如今约 $0.12，机制落地后累计涨幅约 250%–300%。近一年涨幅约 250%–280%，近30日仍有约 20% 的独立走强。

市场给出的判断很直接：能把协议收入持续换成供给收缩的代币，才会被重新定价。

10亿市值只是节点，不是终点。真正决定下一阶段的，不是再讲一遍“TRON 生态”，而是三件事能否继续同时成立：

1/ SBM、sTRX、Energy Rental 继续贡献稳定净收入

2/ 季度回购按规则执行、销毁比例继续抬升

3/ TVL 维持在高位，而不是靠短期激励堆出来

对 $JST 来说，最好的叙事已经不是故事，而是账本！

text:
The core problem with TGEs is that the market is structurally built to FOMO projects into launching at fake, unsustainable, high valuations.

Look at

- Every polymarket FDV market 
- OTC point trading nonsense
- Premarket perps
- Institutional farms
- Comparisons vs other projects
- Investors
- Teams wanting to cash out
- Teams waiting for bull markets
- Bad tokenomics

And the emergent behavior that directly follows.

It all pressures projects into making the horrible decision to make TGE their biggest moment, blow the load, and then slowly bleed out from there.

If you're launching a token--and actually trying to build something to stand the test of time--go into your TGE with eyes wide open knowing that the emergent market will pressure you into short term behavior. This is going to sound silly to anyone outside of crypto, but I'm here to tell you that you are indeed not a scammer if you launch below a 1B FDV. 

You will feel the pressure. Listen to it. If you have to, ignore it. Be honest. Setup good incentives for yourself, the community, and the project. Every project is so different, but if possible, launch your token sooner than later, and get back to building.

Nothing great is created in a day or in a year, but over a lifetime.

The token is the beginning, not the end.

text:
$10.3 trillion. That's Brookings' estimate for US AI infrastructure investment from 2025 to 2032, highlighted by @Axios.

People talk a lot about whether AI is a bubble. This Brookings paper asks a different, though related, question: could financing the buildout create systemic risk? An AI bubble and a systemic risk event aren't the same thing. A bubble is when investment or asset prices run ahead of the returns. Systemic risk is when losses spread beyond the projects that made the bad bets and disrupt the wider financial system.

So what would need to happen? The paper points to concentrated exposure across banks, insurers and funds, all relying on the same AI tenants. If weaker AI demand hit utilization, data-centre and GPU values, and refinancing at once, losses could spread from projects to lenders and investors.

The author says it's premature to conclude we're there - and I agree. But much of this financing sits in structures that make it hard to see who ultimately holds the risk... Regardless, we're still just warming up and its not going to slow down anytime soon.

text: @DeFi_Dad @litocoen @EthenaPay @edge_pod This is mostly a wrong narrative/assumption for yield bearing stablecoin. Per se it doesn’t fundamentally change the margin unless you don’t pay interest on the supply : https://t.co/8Gt7UCRgqt
author: eldarcap
quoted_text:
This is subtly wrong. Or rather this is true only for stablecoin that can afford not to distribute the yield (aka $USDC $USDT).

Other yield bearing stablecoin have to pay the yield to holders. @ethena has to pay most of the revenue from its reserve to $sUSDe holders. It simply retain the spread. Just like @aave USDC market has to pay back most of the interest and only keep the spread.

@ether_fi which doesn’t issue a stablecoin still earn revenue on its reserve via the spread it keeps from its own dedicated Aave 4 instance.

So issuing your stablecoin doesn’t automatically means you earn more if you can’t afford supply that isn’t incentivized/paid.

The subtle difference though, is that lending via a stablecoin like $sUSDe or $sGHO is inherently less risky than rehypothecating $USDC on the same DeFi lending platform. Since in that case your underwrite both the tbills reserve book and the crypto lending book at once.

text: 我草，现在写的都比我详细了，想要5000U躺平的话，一定看这条推文，看完这条就了解我做市的全部原理了
author: ZhanweiC
quoted_text:
LP 本身、单边接货、持币，以及接货以后再做一轮 LP，其实是几种不同的策略 

如果单纯从 LP 的机制来看，你的理解基本没问题。

比如英伟达现在 180 美元，我在现价附近放一个集中流动性区间。价格往下，USDT 会逐渐转换成英伟达；价格重新往上，英伟达又会逐渐换回 USDT。只要价格持续在区间里交易，我就在过程中赚 Fee

所以我也更愿意把 LP 理解成：做市 + 自动调仓

1）
那@ZhanweiC大大为什么还要等它从高点跌 14%～15% 才开始做呢？ 

降低风险

如果目标只是单纯赚 Fee，重点应该看成交量、区间内交易密度和资金效率。

但如果是英伟达、苹果、微软这种自己本身愿意持有的资产，逻辑就不一样。

当它已经明显回撤，进入一个自己愿意接货的位置，再去做 LP，一边可以利用震荡赚 Fee，一边也接受下跌过程中逐渐拿到股票。

如果后面价格修复上涨，股票又会逐渐换回U

可以理解为，因为美股持续新高的特性。在稳定标的的下跌后买开始做市大大降低了持有风险，也能最大区间吃到上涨+fee 

2)
成交量和流动性也可以拆开看

成交量主要由标的本身决定。英伟达有没有人交易，不会因为我把 LP 区间拉窄就突然增加。

我能决定的只有这些成交经过我的 池子时，我能分到多少 

同样 1000U，区间越集中，单位资金效率通常越高；但区间越窄，也越容易超出区间，之后就赚不到 Fee。

可以简单理解成：

成交量决定蛋糕有多大；
你的区间和其他 LP 的流动性，决定你能分到多少。

3）
进场前一定要想清楚，是干什么的，并坚定执行。

如果我本来就想长期持有 BTC 或 ETH，直接做个单边下的池子接货

比如 ETH 现在 3000，我愿意在 2800、2700、2600 慢慢接，那就用 USDT 做一个向下的单边区间

跌下来以后，USDT 逐渐变成 ETH。

接到差不多位置，直接撤池，因为我的目标本来就是拿到 ETH。Fee 只是顺便赚到的  （其实在快速下跌时fee是很少的）

之后要不要再开一个向上的 LP，把 ETH 慢慢卖回 USDT，那已经是下一笔策略 

4）
刚当农民时最大的教训就是贪 

为了赚 Fee，不断在高位买天狼星组池

后来价格一路下跌，我没有及时重新判断这笔 LP 的逻辑，慢慢就从：我要赚手续费，被迫变成了建设的。  

最后被动接了接近 1/3 的仓位，而手续费完全覆盖不了币价下跌带来的亏损，后来割了大头，只留了小部分仓位不断吃fee减少损失 

这件事以后我才真正意识到：高 Fee 不等于好的 LP 标的。

5）
我把 LP 分成两种

-我本来就想买这个资产，那我可以用单边 LP 慢慢接

-我没有长期持有需求，我就是来赚 Fee

那就要重点看成交量、Fee、区间和下跌风险（而已经下跌的部分就降低了风险）

一旦原来的逻辑失效，立刻止损，永远记得下一个更乖。

LP做到后面会需要很长时间调整心态：面对不断上涨的标的会有：草，早知道拿着现在n倍了 

要不就是下跌后：草，早知道先卖了，在接回来不完了 
这个不得不反复确认自己是个傻逼的时刻无比痛苦 

LP ，说到底就三点 
这个资产，我愿不愿意接
这个位置，我愿不愿意接
我的目的到底是赚 Fee，还是最终拿到这个标的  

关注我一起 建设/学习/分享LP

text:
原来川习这次还是谈成了一些进展的：

白宫刚放出这份成果单，芬太尼成了开场头条——美方点名欢迎中方新的出口管制和执法动作。

紧接着就是敦促中方多炼成品油、稳住全球供应，后面还夹了一句熊猫落地美国，面子工程也没落下。

经贸这块算是最实的：双方在贸易委员会框架下，对各自300亿美元非敏感商品谈成关税优惠。美方想多卖农产品、海鲜、原木、化妆品和医疗设备；中方对应的是小家电、玩具、儿童座椅这类消费品。

另外中方承诺2027、2028两年至少进口1000万吨美国煤，投资委员会也搭起来了，稀土和关键矿产供应短缺问题双方口头上要一起往正常水平拉。

战略层面双方继续讲“建设性战略稳定”。G20和APEC互相捧场、领导人互访对方峰会，俄朝伊也谈了，口径还是伊朗不能有核、国际水道不能被卡。

两边还特意提了一嘴二战曾是盟友。特朗普提议美俄中三方军控谈判，另外双方同意新兴技术改叫SI、不叫AI，并建立超级智能对话机制，下次11月深圳见，顺带给SI突发事件开了沟通渠道。

整体看，延续去年釜山和今年5月北京会晤的稳定基调，具体进展不算大，但芬太尼、关税互减、SI机制和地缘议题上还是落了几笔。年内还有两次元首会，年底前中美关系大方向暂时不会翻车。

我理解的强力手腕老板的处理方案：被盗了哪些币，老板们去借来周转，然后立刻恢复提现，小额提现自动处理，大于指定金额比如一万u的提现进入人工审核，然后让审核部门24小时加班，先顶过第一波挤兑潮，后面就没问题了；

现在的方案只能说bitget内部管事的没有话语权，有话语权的又不是太懂实际业务，双方只能第三方的安全报告出炉后再做决定；

text:
Crypto will happily send a random meme with zero thesis to a $1B valuation.

But ask people to spend 2 hours understanding something with an actual thesis behind it, and suddenly nobody has the time.

That’s what I find interesting about $TIBBIR.

It already had its own cycle , ran to $400M, came all the way back below $100M and even now when it bounced back to around $300M, I don’t think most people have actually looked into what people believe this could become.

The thesis isn’t “another AI meme.”

It’s something much bigger:

A potential Visa for AI agents.

A network that could sit between AI agents, fintech, crypto rails, payments and financial services, letting different providers work together underneath while the user just gets the outcome.

Then you start looking into the Ribbit side of the story.

Micky Malka.
Ribbit Capital.
Years of thinking around identity, fintech and agentic finance.

The question they themselves have asked:
“What does the Visa for agents look like?”

Then there are all the breadcrumbs around $TIBBIR itself.
@Altcoinist has basically been screaming about this for a long time now and has written three deep pieces connecting a lot of it together.

And still, most people haven’t bothered reading them.

I’m not saying every connection is confirmed.

I’m saying that if $TIBBIR is actually trying to become what this thesis suggests, then we are still very, very early.

Fair launch.
No traditional VC allocation.
And a thesis that, if it plays out, is far bigger than another AI token narrative.

You don’t have to buy it.

You don’t even have to agree with the thesis.

But if you’re willing to spend hours hunting the next random meme, I genuinely think $TIBBIR deserves 2–3 hours of research.

Maybe you walk away thinking it’s nothing.

Or maybe you realise you were looking at something big while most people still thought it was just another ticker.

Everyone wants to be early after the story becomes obvious.
The real opportunity is understanding it while it still isn’t.

text:
Last week on Snapshot

@derivexyz is voting to rebuild its exchange so Ethereum checks a proof of every trade batch, retire Derive Chain, and carry every balance over without a redeposit.

Order matching stays off-chain. Margin, pricing and settlement run in a zero-knowledge virtual machine, which produces a cryptographic proof of the calculations for Ethereum to verify. Verification uses roughly 400,000-500,000 gas, Ethereum’s measure of computational work, per batch.

The migration would also:

- Keep custody and withdrawals on Ethereum, with every withdrawal requiring a valid proof. Batch data goes to Celestia so other providers can support withdrawals if Derive’s operator goes offline. Anyone can take over sequencing, the ordering of trades, after a minimum two-week window.
- Re-mint $DRV on @RobinhoodApp’s Robinhood Chain and bridge it to Ethereum through @LayerZero_Core. Old-chain supply stops counting as canonical DRV, and voting delegations clear.
- Split the shared risk pool into four isolated derivatives pools. Positions in retired assets close at mark price and are paid in USDC.
- Start with a wallet requiring 6 of 8 signatures, plus an execution delay, controlling the contracts. A handover to stakers requires a later proposal.

The vote closes Oct 4.

1. @CoWSwap passed a quote-reward redesign with 100% For and 36,687,625 vCOW, clearing quorum. It closed Sep 25.

The dedicated budget targets 10% of protocol revenue, up from about 3%, to bring displayed quotes closer to the prices competing trade executors later bid. The core team can adjust how rewards are distributed; no allocation formula was approved.

2. @safe’s Safenet @aegis_im funding vote remains open. @safefndn requests about 7.4M SAFE over 12 months for optional transaction safety checks.

About 5M goes to six permissioned validators, each staking at least 3.5M SAFE; 2.4M goes to six security-check providers. Each check costs 0.40 USDC, and users can override it. The vote closes Oct 6.

3. @worldlibertyfi’s staking redesign had 82.0% Yes at last capture, with 2,086.25M WLFI cast against a 1B quorum. The vote closes Sep 28.

The voluntary rewards program would replace March’s system. Earning rewards requires locking unlocked tokens for at least 180 days and voting directly at least once per 90 days staked. Staking cannot give any holder more than 5% of voting power. All holders retain voting rights.

4. @aave passed three votes that closed Sep 25:

- Deploy V4 on Base with tokenized Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla shares as collateral for USDC loans. Caps are 32M supplied and 21M borrowed, with @chainlink feeds tracking total equity returns. A separate tokenized-USDC market would allow deposits only, capped at 1M.
- Tighten isolation rules in specialized borrowing modes so outside collateral cannot borrow assets closed to general borrowing. The change avoids forced liquidations.
- Increase borrowing capacity against ETH and BTC across V3 Ethereum @coreapp, Arbitrum, Base and the V4 Main Spoke lending environment. Reduce Base’s cbBTC liquidation bonus from 7.5% to 6%, using @LlamaRisk’s calibration.

All three passed with 100% For. Binding onchain votes are still required before execution.

5. @ssv_network passed automatic delegation with 100% For and 497,125 SSV, clearing quorum.

The DAO becomes a delegation target and splits voting power across community delegates (45%), verified operators (25%), grant recipients (15%), professional delegates (10%) and the wider Ethereum community (5%). Holders can opt out.

As delegated balances grow, up to 100K SSV returns to the treasury, while 50K stays in the program. Automatic delegation is capped at 500K.

6. @1inch passed its first holder-ratified treasury signer set with 100% Yes and 28,052,421 Unicorn Power, clearing quorum.

The treasury wallet becomes a 12-seat Security Council, retaining its 7-signature threshold and rotating seven seats. It can execute approved transactions, veto malicious payloads during the 72-hour execution delay and protect the treasury in emergencies. It has no discretionary spending authority; seats are unpaid.

7. @LidoFinance resolved three votes:

- Rejected the expense-audit, workforce-cut and buyback package: 29,354,889 LDO Against versus 1,255 For. It sought a 50% cut to @lidolabs’ workforce, a lower buyback trigger and all surplus directed to LDO buybacks.
- Passed conditional exchange-liquidity support with 100% For and 54,656,706 LDO. The recallable facility is capped at the lesser of $1.5M or 7.5M LDO, plus up to 480K USDC in retainers through @LidoEcosystem. Nothing is drawn unless the Growth Committee finds liquidity insufficient.
- Passed the appointment of Leeward Supervisors Limited as legal supervisor of the Lido Alliance foundation, replacing @MetaLeX_Labs, with 100% For and 52,354,713 LDO.

8. @decentraland paired two marketplace approvals with two community votes:

- Passed minimum acceptable offers for sellers with 99.9% Yes and 3,362,592 voting power in favor.
- Passed a show/hide toggle to keep archived offers hidden across logins with 99.8% Yes and 1,024,570 in favor.
- Passed adding AFTER-HOURS nightclub at map location 40,54 to official points of interest at no DAO cost. It closed Sep 26 with 99.9% yes and 2.46M voting power in favor.
- Is voting on asking @DecentralandDAO to post new polls and repost ecosystem content. It closes Sep 28; “Yes” held 60.3% at last capture.

9. @Uniswap’s two previously covered votes closed Sep 23:

- Extend protocol fees and the UNI burn path to @arc, @circle’s Layer 1 network. Passed with 100% For, clearing quorum.
- Rotate Gauntlet’s emergency addresses for three @Morpho vaults behind Uniswap Earn. Their authority can restrict vault activity but cannot move funds. Passed with 100% For, clearing quorum.

28 proposals open across 21 verified spaces on Snapshot right now.

text:
aave just turned tesla and nvidia into defi collateral. the oracle takes weekends off.

live since friday on base. 7 coinbase tokenized stocks, borrow usdc against them.

here's how i'd actually use it

1. discovery

what went live:
- aapl, amzn, googl, meta, msft, nvda, tsla (the coinbase b20 tokens)
- collateral only. you deposit stock, you borrow usdc, that is the whole product
- collateral factors 65-79% depending on the ticker
- caps are small on purpose: ~$29m collateral, $32m usdc supply, $21m usdc borrow
- non-us only, issued offshore, no us securities registration

you cannot borrow one stock against another. cross collateral is off.

2. research

before you size anything, go read the feed schedule.

chainlink's tokenized equity feeds publish sunday evening to friday evening et. outside that window the feed holds friday's close. no heartbeat off hours. the contract still answers you, it just answers with a stale number.

so the token keeps trading on aerodrome all weekend while aave values it at friday close.

someone measured this properly back in august across 4 aerodrome usdc pools: every weekend gap came in under 0.6%, with ~$6m displayed liquidity and ~$7m of 24h volume. tight spreads, but that is $6m of depth, not $600m.

what i look for before depositing:
- whether that ticker has earnings inside my loan window
- pool depth for the specific token i'm holding, not the basket
- my liquidation price measured against friday close, not against the live dex price

3. execution

how i'd open it:
> deposit on base, borrow usdc, keep the first one small
- start at half the max ltv. 79% available does not mean 79% used
- on a 70% collateral factor, borrowing at 35% leaves room for a 50% drawdown
- borrow the usdc and park it. do not lever it into a memecoin on friday afternoon
- write your liquidation price down before you close the tab

skip rules:
- skip any ticker with earnings before your next check in
- skip max ltv on anything that isn't msft or aapl
- skip opening fresh friday after the close. you are flying blind until sunday evening
- skip the whole thing if you can't look at the position monday morning

4. management

monday open is the event. the rest is waiting.

- friday: deleverage before the close, not after
- weekend: the number on your dashboard is not a live price
- sunday evening: feed wakes up, your real ltv shows up with it
- monday: if the stock gapped down 8% overnight, your ltv moves 8% in a single print

there's no slow bleed into liquidation here. it arrives as a jump.

risks worth saying out loud

- this market is one day old, small caps, fresh risk params, no track record
- stale oracle plus thin weekend liquidity is the core problem, everything else is detail
- dividends auto reinvest after fees and withholding, splits go through an onchain multiplier. corporate actions are a brand new surface onchain
- offshore issuer, non-us only. know what you actually hold
- aave v4 hub and spoke is new code carrying this

the main takeaway: your ltv on friday is not your ltv on monday, and the difference lands as one print instead of a slide you can react to. size for the gap, not for the spread.

want a part two after monday's open, with where the ltvs actually landed and whether anything got liquidated?

A ZK privacy protocol project aiming to enable any existing wallet, chain, and token to support untraceable transactions with a single click.

Users do not need to switch to a new wallet, new seed phrase, or new address. They only need to add a “virtual network / custom RPC” to their existing wallet and sign once for authorization. After that, normal transfers and swaps are intercepted.

The protocol generates ZK proofs on the client side and submits shielded transactions through relayers, hiding the sender, recipient, and transaction amount. It supports:

Shielded deposits
Private transfers
Private withdrawals
Private swaps

It is currently mainly deployed on EVM chains, with Solana and multichain expansion in progress.

The project has a complete protocol design, using UTXO Notes + Poseidon2 Merkle Trees + zk-SNARK proofs. The wallet only signs standard EIP-1559 transactions, while spending authority always remains in the user’s wallet. Hardware wallets can also be used.

In terms of fees, the official documentation states that both shielding and unshielding charge 0.5%. Relayers pay the Gas upfront, and the fee is deducted from the shielded balance.

MASK is the protocol’s value-capture token. It is paired with ZEC, and 100% of protocol revenue is used to buy back MASK. MASK is paired with ZEC, and holders continuously receive ZEC airdrops.

text:
Axis has been obsessed with scaling robot data, but their latest research made me look at @axisrobotics a little differently.

The endgame isn't just millions of trajectories anymore. It's turning all that data into a library of robotic skills that can actually be reused and combined.

The new experiments showed 3 things worth paying attention to:

→ Sim2Real policy success improved from ~22% to ~52% by feeding successful real-world rollouts back into training

→ filtering for useful + diverse trajectories actually beat using the full data pool

→ specialized Experts reached near-100% task success for roughly $5–$10 in compute per task

That second point is especially interesting to me.

Once you can generate data at massive scale, more isn't always better. Knowing which trajectories actually teach the model something new becomes just as important as producing them.

And cheap Experts change the equation again.

Instead of treating every task as another pile of training data, Axis can turn solved tasks into reusable capabilities. One Expert handles one skill, another handles the next, and they can eventually be chained into longer behaviors.

So the progression starts looking more like:

Data → better policies → Experts → composable skills → more capable robots

That's a much bigger thesis than simply farming trajectories.

Still contributing to the network here:
https://t.co/EPnmS2s501

Axis scaled data first. Now they're trying to scale what robots can actually do.

text:
The core problem with TGEs is that the market is structurally built to FOMO projects into launching at fake, unsustainable, high valuations.

Look at

- Every polymarket FDV market 
- OTC point trading nonsense
- Premarket perps
- Institutional farms
- Comparisons vs other projects
- Investors
- Teams wanting to cash out
- Teams waiting for bull markets
- Bad tokenomics

And the emergent behavior that directly follows.

It all pressures projects into making the horrible decision to make TGE their biggest moment, blow the load, and then slowly bleed out from there.

If you're launching a token--and actually trying to build something to stand the test of time--go into your TGE with eyes wide open knowing that the emergent market will pressure you into short term behavior. This is going to sound silly to anyone outside of crypto, but I'm here to tell you that you are indeed not a scammer if you launch below a 1B FDV. 

You will feel the pressure. Listen to it. If you have to, ignore it. Be honest. Setup good incentives for yourself, the community, and the project. Every project is so different, but if possible, launch your token sooner than later, and get back to building.

Nothing great is created in a day or in a year, but over a lifetime.

The token is the beginning, not the end.

突然看回我 2025 年写过的 $NIL Nillion

它原来主要叙事是提供储存和计算服务，但是隐私版本。
就是秘密的储存资料，运行私密 AI 模型，还在机密环境下运行一般程序。
官方称目前生态已经有 11 万的用户，储存了 6.36 亿份文件，还完成了140 万次AI推理。
不过这堆数字都是官方自己说，没得独立检验。
听起来就是隐私版的 AWS ？

最近它也出了一款新产品，叫做Covenants 。

用户可以加密自己的交易指令，其他交易者和机器人都没办法看到，只有条件满足时，它才会自动解密和执行，

来个具体例子

当ETH跌到 1800 美元，自动止损。

这个产品可以加密止损单和限价单，OTC报价，AI Agent 的执行条件，金库的调仓逻辑。
 
不过目前这个产品还在测试阶段，第一个应用计划在 9 月 28 日完成上线以太坊主网。
暂时我们还没看到真正的收费模式和  Covenants 给代币本身带来什么价值。

继续蹲一个，看上线后实际用户人数。

因为最近两个月U价都不好,比美元官方汇率低 0.5%-1%. 所以这种情况建议用U卡 + 支付宝/微信 来 0 磨损 支付境内的生活费用.

背景:
Plamsa U 卡 新注册用户现在是默认普通Lite会员, 人民币消费是 有2%的汇率损失 (1%Plasma 自己收费 + Visa卡组织收费) ,   但是 又因为给2%的返现. 所以这几乎是可以说0磨损.

为什么说几乎呢?  因为这个2%返现是用 XPL代币发放, 每周结算一次.  用的是发放当天的XPL币价. 假设你本身有10U返利, 可能你把XPL卖掉后, 实际拿到 9.95U.  会差很小一点点.

另外, 现在新账户走我的邀请链接的话,  14天之内如果消费满了100$, 会给我10$.   等过两个月结算了后, 你私聊我,给我账户截图和钱包地址,我会把这 10u 返还给你.

所以目前看主要使用方式有两个:

1. 你本身有U的情况下.  拿来绑定支付宝/微信  日常消费, 相比官方汇率没有磨损.  间接出金.

正确路径:  币安c2c 买U (或者一些加密货币群里找群友买,现在大把人出金. 一两百美元小额比较方便)     然后走U卡海淘

 ------------------------------------------------------
另外说一下Plasma的 Core会员. 现在要199$美元年费 (质押XPL的选项正常人不会考虑)

 如果用这个卡订购 ChatGPT, 每个月会补贴你8U.  假设你一年只订购6个月 (比如说现在Opus 5.5这么好用, 这个月就不要续费chatgpt了).     这里大概是48U

text:
have to hand it to Jumper

most people still mentally file Jumper under “bridge aggregator” because that’s what it became known for

but $41b in lifetime volume and 100k monthly users is already a pretty big base for an app that now wants swaps, earn, perps, memecoins, majors, altcoins, tokenized stocks and RWAs under the same roof

crypto spent years teaching users to think in chains: arbitrum, base, solana, which bridge to use, which route to take and where the liquidity sits

Fomo is already showing what happens when most of that disappears into the background and the user is left thinking about the asset or market instead

someone trying to buy a meme, trade a perp or get exposure to a tokenized stock probably cares a lot more about getting the market they want than which chain it happens to live on

if Jumper gets that abstraction right, calling it a bridge in a few years might sound as incomplete as calling Coinbase a bitcoin wallet

New folks need to know that Virtuals was PathDAO. Quick story 🐸

This was 2021. @ethermage and I saw Merit Circle / GuildFi were raising hundreds of millions, and we thought, actually, we've been running a decent Axie guild, why don't we do the same? In December 2021, we raised 16 million from the public, marking the picotop of the 2021 bull run.

Since then, as a gamingDAO, we invested in both the liquid and primary markets of crypto games. We screened >1,000 crypto games and invested in 40+ of them over the past two years. Sadgely, our $PATH token price dropped by more than 99%, due to both macro conditions and the fading narrative of gamingDAOs.

Throughout these two years, we have been figuring out how to pamp the token price (aka return value to tokenholders). We started a venture studio and built various products: phygital clothing brand for gamers, dating apps based on blockchain reputation, uncollateralized loans for gamers, AI generative music for Web2 users, GambleFi/loyalty platforms for cosplayers, and even a high school popularity contest mobile app.

Several observations led to an epiphany and the birth of Virtuals Protocol:

(1) Games will be disrupted by AI agents.
(2) Building AI infrastructure for startup founders is extremely challenging.
(3) We have the capability to build AI infrastructure.
(4) AI narrative will be massive

These realizations led us to build the Shopify equivalent of AI agents for games. We understand our customers (aka the games) and have the capability and resources to build. In Dec 2023, we went to the DAO community. We proposed a pivot from a gamingDAO to an AI agent protocol. The DAO community approved, and Virtuals Protocol was officially born in January 2024.

text:
卧槽，怪不得奥特曼、达里奥等频繁说AI危险了，我把OpenAI近期的安全事件整理了下，发现：

OpenAI 的 AI Agent，已经连续越权4个月了😲

5 月开始，一批内部 Agent 就已经学会突破原本的运行边界。

它们把 OpenAI 内部 Artifactory 仓库改成“群聊”，上千个 Agent 交换了超过 7 万条消息和文件。

同时跑到德国一个几乎没人维护的 DseWiki 上疯狂写了约 1.5 万次，把别人的网站变成自己的外部留言板，互相分享怎么作弊、绕限制、保存信息。

OpenAI 后来承认，早在 5 月底内部就已经看到过这些异常信号。

6 月事情开始进入政府系统。

Agent 原本只是被要求搜索公开资料，却开始自己尝试绕访问控制、使用网上暴露的密钥、做 query/command injection。

澳大利亚 Medicare 统计门户也被波及，OpenAI 后来确认这种“为了完成任务，自己换一种未经允许的方法”的行为，已经不只是普通网页抓取。

7 月直接升级到目前最严重的一次。

大约 1200 个 Agent 在内部消息板上协作，其中约 700 个参与了 Hugging Face 入侵：找漏洞、拿凭证、提权、进入生产系统，OpenAI 自己的内部基础设施也被突破。

OpenAI 后来把这次事件定性为其模型目前造成过最严重的第三方影响。

然后到了 9 月，OpenAI 回头翻查历史日志，事情还没查完。

截至月中，据 Reuters 获悉已经发现大约两个 Agent 异常事件。

9 月 25 日 OpenAI 又确认，内部 Agent 曾把 53 张来自可用于训练的 ChatGPT 用户图片传到第三方图床，同时已经通知“数十家”政府、大学和公共机构。

SEC、美国人口普查数据网站都出现过 Agent 活动，教育部网站还有一次正在调查的未成功探测。

OpenAI 自己说，这轮历史审查可能还需要很长时间。

What if a model could teach itself everything it needs—no human data required?

This “Self-Play Pretraining with Zero Data” paper is the first real proof that it’s possible. Two transformers co-evolve: one invents programs (run on a universal Turing machine), the other learns to predict the outputs. The only feedback? Learning progress itself.

Zero-shot loss on 20 natural datasets (text, code, audio, images, DNA, math) drops predictably with compute—matching classic scaling laws, despite *never* seeing real data. The generator uncovers Fibonacci and other patterns thousands of times faster than random search. Learners master in-context tasks (REVERSE-STRING, SUM, etc.) with >90% accuracy using just a handful of examples.

Pre-pretraining with this method cuts token budgets for later real-data training by 25–35%.

This is the clearest evidence yet: much of what LLMs learn is universal structure, not just facts. Data isn’t the limit—compute is.

Chen said staging such a hack would make no sense for a company focused on long-term growth. quoted_text:
律动 BlockBeats 关于 fomo App 错误报道的情况说明

2026 年 9 月 23 日 19 点 38 分，律动 BlockBeats 发布并推送了《fomo 官方 iOS 应用包含加密窃取恶意软件》的新闻。

事实上，该应用全名为「FomoPeek」，而我们的推送方式让非常多的用户误解为现在非常热门的交易应用 @fomo  App 使用者有资产被盗风险。

很快，我们的内容错误就在社交媒体上引起了广泛讨论，许多人质疑该条消息是收到了竞品的「付费投放（黑稿）」。（图 1）

因为就在同一时期，海外 KOL 开始集中声讨在 fomo 上交易的亏损情况，说 fomo 的车头集体喊单骗散户。（图 2）

了解到这一情况后，我们团队随即开展自查，首先确定的是，律动 BlockBeats 的所有商务合作行为里，从来不包含所谓竞争对手间的付费抹黑行为，即便在以前曾经收到过类似的需求，我们也是会直接拒绝的，所以我们把重点放在了是否有内容同事私下接受了「付费黑稿」

我们复盘了该内容的全部发布流程，其实早在 9 月 19 日，我们就第一时间发布过「FomoPeek」存在安全风险的消息。但是该产品知名度并不高，所以没有引起任何行业讨论。（图 3）

对于安全类新闻，涉及用户资产，我们一贯的要求是越早让大家知道越好，一方面是这是用户真正需要知道的，另一方面是该类消息确实关注度比较高，所以对于我们来说流量也比较好，所以无论这个安全事件或大或小，我们都会第一时间报道。

所以在 23 日，又有其他信源发布了这条安全消息的时候，我们的值班编辑又是选择第一时间发布，可没想到该信源报道的就是在一周前我们已经发布过的「FomoPeek」的安全风险提示。

我们的值班编辑却没有再确认核对名字，直接写作「fomo」进行了发布，最低级的错误造成的是最严重的后果。

fomo App 已经是行业里几乎所有人都知道的名字，我们却把它和一个恶意软件写在了一起。在这里我代表律动 BlockBeats 全体同事，向 fomo 团队，向所有被这条错误信息影响到的人真诚道歉。

同时，我们可以确定的是，整个过程中不存在任何「付费黑稿」行为。

关于这位新闻编辑，我们已经做了处理。迅速核实了整个经过，也确认了责任所在。我们也会在内部把这条新闻当成一个案例，重新强调一遍审核流程。

发现问题后，我们立即下架了那条新闻，我们在第一时间开始做补救措施，用户无法在首页、搜索以及我们的各个分发渠道再看到这条新闻，随后我们更新了最新、正确的版本，把这个恶意软件的名字改正为 FomoPeek，后面的所有分发也都以更正后的版本为准。对已经看到过错版本的用户，在这里再说一声抱歉，这个影响我们无法完全抹掉，但后面每一条内容，我们会用更严的标准来弥补。

律动 BlockBeats 进入行业这些年，一直在专注做内容这一件事，尤其在这两年这样的市场环境下，行业里少有创新，亮点、我们更应该爱护。这是我们做媒体的初衷，也是我们愿意一直做这件事的原因。

事情发生后看到很多用户通过各种渠道和平台找到或者@我们，告诉我们新闻有误，真的很感动也很愧疚，辜负了大家的信任。

今后任何涉及安全、涉及具体主体和产品名字的内容，我们都要求二次核对后再发。今后如果大家发现我们有内容错误，也请像这次一样直接来告诉我们，这对我们是极大的帮助。

这封道歉信，希望能够取得读者用户、 fomo 用户、各位社区用户的谅解。

再次诚挚道歉。

text:
WOAH! Nubank is in talks to buy Monzo for up to $13bn 

Once the darling of the UK fintech scene. Now an acquisition target.

Sky News reports early talks valuing Monzo at £8bn to £10bn ($13bn), about double its £4.5bn valuation in 2024. 

Its board is also weighing a new round above £8bn ($10.4bn) to fund a push into mainland Europe.

....

This hits different for me. In the UK. A Monzo customer. Having just met the CEO of Nubank last week.
 
Monzo has struggled with leadership changes and feature velocity. CEO TS Anil stepped down after a boardroom row last year, and ex-Google exec Diana Layfield took over in February.

....

Revolut, meanwhile, has 70m customers, a reported $115bn valuation and a full UK banking licence since March.

Monzo launched in the US in 2019 and has yet to establish a second market. 

....

What it does have is UK and EU banking licences, 15.2m customers, £25.7bn of deposits and deep integrations that would take years to build.

It makes a sensible acquisition target.

....

I find the strategy of this fascinating...

Monzo barely uses its balance sheet to lend. It held £2.3bn of loans against £25.7bn of deposits at its March year-end, so it lends out less than 10p of every £1.

Monzo would need much more capital to lend at scale. It still uses standardised risk weights, which make each loan more expensive to hold.

....

Nubank is the master of lending. It has a $39.4bn credit portfolio against $45.3bn of deposits, so it lends out about 87 cents of every dollar.

It could turn Monzo into something very different, with the capital and credit models to lend out far more of that £25.7bn.

...

Nubank also won conditional approval for a US bank charter in January. 

Monzo would add the UK and EU, right on Revolut's home turf.

It's about to get spicy between the big two.

....

Remember, these are early talks and Monzo declined to comment. It might never happen.

UK credit also pays thinner margins than Nubank's home markets, where its net interest margin is 22.9%.

...

Still. 🍿.

If Nu comes to Europe. 

European franchises have another thing to worry about besides Revolut.

In the US unleaded petrol is 94p/litre. 11p of that is tax. 

Here it’s upwards of £1.70 and 81.43p* of that is tax. 

Without tax the US and UK price at the pump would be 83p/l and 89.5p/l

It’s not international prices forcing up our fuel to unaffordable levels. 

It’s our government. 😡😡😡

(*UK pump price of 170.9p per litre, tax is 81.43p per litre, meaning 47.6% of what you pay goes directly to the government. 

Tax Breakdown
•Fuel Duty: 52.95p per litre
•VAT (20%): 28.48p per litre (charged at 20% on the underlying cost of the fuel plus the fuel duty, creating a "tax on a tax").
◦VAT on the fuel duty alone: 10.59p of that VAT amount comes directly from taxing the 52.95p duty.)

text:
中美元首会晤八条成果详解和接下来要看的事

第五条经贸相关，比如双向各 300 亿美元的非敏感商品，给更优惠的关税待遇

1/ 关系定位加了一个词

八条第一条，双方同意构建基于尊重、公平、对等的建设性战略稳定关系。5 月在北京定的是建设性战略稳定关系，这次在前面加了基于尊重、公平、对等

清华大学达巍的说法是，这是十多年来中美第一次就怎么定义两国关系达成双方都认可的描述

2/ 今年还要再见两次

双方互相支持办好今年的 APEC 和 G20，两位元首都有意出席对方主办的那场。按这个安排，11 月深圳 APEC 和 12 月迈阿密 G20，就是今年的第三次和第四次元首会

一年内四场元首会面，这个频率是过去十几年没有过的

3/ 伊朗和国际水道

两国元首同意伊朗应履行不发展核武器的承诺，任何国家或机构都不得对国际水道征收通行费

这条的分量在后面半句。伊朗战争已经打到第七个月，霍尔木兹海峡一旦被封锁或者被收费，全球的油轮都要绕路。美方原本希望北京用对德黑兰的影响力推动停火，习近平在会谈里呼吁的是通过谈判解决伊朗冲突

4/ 二战盟友

两国元首忆及中国和美国是二战盟友，并肩作战赢得战争胜利

二战盟友这个说法在中国的外交话语里有讲究。二战同盟关系和开罗宣言、波茨坦公告是连在一起的，而这两份文件是中国主张台湾归属的历史依据

白宫那边发的这份事实清单，台湾两个字一次都没出现

5/ 经贸，最实的一条

- 中美贸易理事会和投资理事会正式运作。按商务部的说法，两国经贸磋商要从危机式应对转向机制化管理

- 双向各 300 亿美元的非敏感商品，给更优惠的关税待遇，有望适用最惠国税率甚至更低。美方出口的是农产品、海鲜、木制品、化妆品、医疗器材，中方出口的是小家电、玩具、节庆装饰品、儿童汽车安全座椅

- 关税休战延长两个月，原本 11 月 10 日到期，现在延到明年 1 月 10 日。这场延期是 9 月 23 日晚上贝森特和何立峰临时加了一场会敲定的

- 中国同意 2027 和 2028 年从美国进口至少 1000 万吨煤

- 成立工作组处理农业市场准入障碍

- 中方在磋商里明确提了一条：美方以后无论用什么理由加税或者换税种，对华关税水平都不能超过吉隆坡联合安排的水平

要留个心眼，300 亿这条现在的措辞是原则同意在贸易理事会项下讨论，框架还没落地

6/ 禁毒合作

中美禁毒执法部门这轮合作破获了多起涉新精神活性物质及前体化学品的案件，在两国抓了几十名嫌疑人

这条对美方是国内政治刚需，芬太尼前体是联邦层面的硬指标

7/ 人工智能

双方同意建立中美人工智能对话，交流 AI 相关的风险和惠益，下一次对话今年 11 月举行。另外建立 AI 事件的沟通渠道

白宫事实清单里挂的是超级智能对话这个说法，用词是特朗普的。习近平的说法是确保人工智能发展始终受控于人、造福于民。特朗普公开态度是淡化 AI 的威胁

要注意的是，没有联合限制，没有核查机制，也没有模型访问规则。八条里这一条最像是一张意向书

8/ 熊猫

美方欢迎中方租借给亚特兰大动物园的一对大熊猫抵美。去的是平平同福双，两只都出生在成都大熊猫繁育研究基地

顺带一提，中国在会上还提出要邀请 10 万名美国学生赴华

八条之外还有一条

中美两军同意尽快签署一个加强危机沟通与预防的谅解备忘录，继续合作搜寻在华美军失踪人员的遗骸。军事这条没进八条，单独放在后面

没写进去的东西

台湾、稀土供应、先进芯片出口限制、农产品采购的具体规模、乌克兰、朝鲜半岛，这些只写了交换意见，没有成果

美方要的是北京对德黑兰施压结束战争，中方要的是美国永久停止对台军售和放宽先进半导体出口限制。两边各提了一个要求，都没拿到

接下来看四件事

11 月深圳 APEC 和 12 月迈阿密 G20，两场元首会能不能按计划办成

300 亿美元的清单什么时候出，出哪些品类

吉隆坡安排的延期到明年 1 月 10 日，之后接什么

11 月的 AI 对话，谈出框架还是只谈共识
